name: Celeste Ruppelt
text:
Interesting Place to visit  to see the damage open pit mining does to the land. $2 Adult Admission allows one to stand or sit on a shaded viewing platform above the 'lake' formed when the mine's pumps were shut off in 1982. The water has been back-filling ever since. The level is now approaching the ground water levels. The water is caustic, but there is no access to it and it does not smell. Listen to a recorded video while you observe.
There is a nice 'park-like' area provided by the Anaconda, the mining company; free-parking, nicely landscaped plantings, clean restrooms, and a covered, breezy picnic area.
There is also a Gift Shop where some amazing copper items are displayed.
A good and interesting educational experience.

Summary; perfect trucker rest stop.

It's a nice place all-in-all. It's a bit older of a building, but the rooms are still nice and have typical amenities, such as hidden fridge and HDTV+cable. The sinks are outside the bathroom, which I'm not a fan of personally. Being an older building, it's not as sounds proof as others. The floors echo enough that even light walking can make you sound like a lead-foot to the floor below. Lots of pounding around was heard, and you can hear any time anyone around you uses the water, cause the pipes sing.

Pool is very nice with a small water side - not made for people over 5'5". The hot tub is great, when it works. Over the course of 2 weeks it's been down for maintenance 3 times. And even adults need a wristband - some of which are the concert style; one use only- but you still have to have a band for consecutive use. Really??

Breakfast is good, but not great. The ham is cheap, and the biscuits aren't fresh - they're in the plastic bread display, along with every other bread type that's not the most fresh either. More days with sausage instead of ham would be great ;)

name: Jess Is Blessed
text:
My toddler's, who are 2 and 4 absolutely love the "Splash Park" and are always excited to go.  Plus, it's FREE!!  This place is excellent for families on a budget, or big families who can't afford $50-$100 for a single family outing at some of Bozeman/Belgrade's other attractions.
The hours are great, the park doesn't close really early which is great for long summer days.  There's lots of benches and I never have a hard time finding a spot to sit.
It's very clean, well taken care of and every family and child I've encountered has been respectful, kind and friendly.  There's also a beautiful, well kept park, play area,  and covered BBQ area.  The one thing I think it's lacking is public restrooms,  although I could be wrong, but I've never seen them.
Overall,  I love bringing the little kids to the splash park and the kids look forward to it opening all winter.   I highly, highly recommend this place! 👍

text:
When I first moved in to town, I didn't know where to buy replacement parts for my vehicles.  The staff are very helpful and friendly.  I'm mechanically inclined, but not a petrol-head, and they've helped me figure out some tricky repairs.  Having free use of the diagnostic machine (don't know it's real name) has saved me hundreds in shop repair fees.

So far, they've helped me with:

Complete headlight assembly replacement: Total cost ≈$55 - Repair shop wanted $435
Intake Manifold Gasket replacement: Total cost $4.50 - Repair shop wanted $260
Trailer light replacement: Total cost $9 - Repair shop wanted $120
Fender and hood touch up: Total cost $23 - Repair shop wanted ≈$300

Total spent: ≈$86.50
Total I would have spent: ≈$1,115

Granted, I've had some sweat equity of my own time put in to these repairs, but they've really helped me save a lot - and have been great about it the whole way.

name: Pancasatya Agastra
text: Here we go. So, here are some tips and tricks for Chinatown restaurant. The food is the most fresh during opening and throughout peak lunch time. If you come pretty close during closing time, you will see dried up buffet. HOWEVER, they will make fresh buffet item that is already drying on the buffet. All you need to do is to ASK for the new stuff. The same way with dinner time, but maybe there's no more dinner time. Anything that is not OK with the food, you can ask politely, and they will try to accommodate you. There are regular customers to this place. For new customers, it may be a bit difficult. This place is packed on Sunday with a lot of families. If you dig Chinese food and want to have an event here, just ask if they are willing to accommodate. Few of my friends have had dinner events here. So, good luck! BTW, there are two menus: one is the OG Chinese and the other is the regular menu. You know what I am talking about.

text: No more dinner time buffet, which is a bummer (still has a lunch time buffet), but dinner off the menu was delicious. Food was fresh with variety of flavors and textures (no "brown sauce on everything," thank God), and delicious. The dumplings (potstickers) were tasty; the perfect combination of crisp and steamed, and it's sauce just right. Appetizers and dinner was served in good time. And the fortune cookies were crisp and tasty. It'd been a while since I'd eaten there - it was worth the wait.

text:
SERIOUSLY DO NOT GO HERE. WORST BUFFET EVER. READ OUR EXPERIENCE BELOW:

We waited minutes to be seated and had to walk around to find a host to finally be seated. It was $16 per person. We sat down and after we were seated the waiter did not come back again until she brought the bill. There was one other table there.
The buffet was very small and the dishes they did have out were cold, dry and 1/4 to 1/2 full platters. Some dishes they didn't even bother to refill and put out. For example they had three seperate plates that were suppose to have three kinds of sushi. There was only one out of three kinds of sushi rolls that were out and there was just a few of that kind.The roll had been out so long the rice had hardened and became crunchy. None of the food was hot or fresh. Now I remind you this at 7 and they close at 9. I would of expected this at 8:30 because the restaurant was closing soon, however this was two hours before they close
The final straw was when the icecream machine didn't even work. Now we just paid $31 for the two of us to experience the absolute worst Chinese food, worst buffet, and pretty bad service. How do they charge full price when the icecream machine doesn't work, a lot of the food isn't out, and the stuff that is has been sitting there for hours?

I paid. Then politely told the waiter I was disappointed in these above things and the over all experience. She couldn't understand me so she grabbed her boss. So I repeated my concerns, he didn't respond to me. Instead he started speaking another language to the waiter. Then he told me it's my fault for coming in so late( we were finished and had the bill paid an hour before they closed) and wouldn't take any kind of responsibility. I told him I would not be coming back and left.

name: Megan
text:
Ok, let's be up front: The Korner Klub is in the local paper on the regular for run-ins with the city over sewage issues. HOWEVER - I eat here so often that I lie to my friends about where I am, and I have never had so much as a upset stomach. To the contrary - the buffs are amazing, the salad dressing is on point, the burgers are good enough, and anyone who thinks the $10 steak night is going to be life-changing good deserves the lesson they learn, and they will like the $10 steak ad potato they get because they are still really tasty.

The real charm behind the Korner Klub is that somehow, for a bar with a casino attached, they manage to have an atmosphere where kids can join their parents for a quick meal, and everyone is respectful and nice. The music on the porch during the summer is wonderful.

Staff is always nice, sassy when necessary, and as long as you sit near-ish the main area (the dark corners will not get stellar service on a dead night) you will be fine. Order the regular  and sweet thai buffs 50/50, and make sure to drink local brews.

resp.text: Thank you for your feedback, Bridgette.  I apologize that the driver felt they were not treated fairly.  We have had some frustrations with Grubhub, as they posted our menu without contacting us, creating headaches for us (inaccurate menus on their site, not enough time to execute orders, overwhelming our systems, etc.) so we asked for them to take our menu off their site.We have concerns about their business practices.We partner with the locally owned Delivery.com to do our delivery business.  They work with us to ensure accurate and timely ordering and delivery.  I am not sure how you were able to order through Grubhub, since we don't have a menu with them anymore. Again, we apologize if our frustrations with the larger company were not conveyed professionally to the driver.  We do our best to work well within the community and appreciate the same from our partners.

name: Chad Peterson
text: I always try to rate places in context.  Would I give Fresco 4 stars in a metropolis?  Not likely - but in a tiny town it'd get 5 stars all day long.  Given it's location in a medium sized city - i'll go with 4.  Based on food alone, I'd say 4 bordering on 5 - good food that doesn't stray far from standard Italian cuisine.  The service from our server was ho-hum - friendly when she was there but that was woefully rare (only appearing when, curiously, a wine glass was empty - more on that later).  The prices would be on par for an upscale Italian eatery in Chicago - which, in my opinion, puts it simply too pricey for Bozeman Montana (but they're downtown and catering to a different crowd).  Their house white wine by the glass was $12.  Infer from that what you will - it seemed north of goofy to me.  And finally the parking - as a place downtown, the parking is predictably sparse - which can be an irritation if you're eating with older or handicapped people.  So - good food, meh prices and service in a setting that is, admittedly, spot on (from someone that has traveled Italy) earn Fresco 4 stars - not worth a long drive but worth a stop if you're in Bozeman.

It has an air of fanciness to it that cant be understated, however you will hardly notice that by the cacaphonous roar that seems to drown out everything. Even the person sitting opposite you at the table. The food was very good though all be the prices are quite steep. I would definitely recommend this place for dinner if you have the cash AND catch an outside table. Otherwise steer clear.

name: Debbie Dawson
text: Always good food and service

name: Chris Sedgwick
text: Food is great. Wine pairing wine with the food is fantastic....a little dark with the atmosphere though, but, I love that place.

name: Lynda Andros-Clay
text: Great place to meet friends and have a delicious dinner. Staff is very friendly and knowledgeable.

name: John McParland
text: great mussels and foccacia bread. our server mike was a very friendly and efficient fellow. cant wait to go back!!!

name: Jeremy Swinborne
text: Love eating outside with the sound of the creek running by.

name: Jason Daughenbaugh
text:
One of our top 3 restaurants in Bozeman.

Food and service is always great.  The Patio along Bozeman Creek is fabulous in the warmer months.

name: Jessica Katherine
text: Amazing outdoor atmosphere, great food and drinks too!

resp.text: Thanks, Jessica.  It's so nice to see some signs of Spring.  Hope to see you again, when the sun comes back out!

name: Kris King
text: Fantastic food and service - what else do you need?

resp.text: Exactly!  We love making great food and we're glad it showed!

name: Caleb Salusso
text: Best Italian food ever!  Spaghetti and meatballs is exceptionally good!

resp.text: Thank, Caleb!  Spag and meatballs is a signature!  Glad you like it as much as we do!

name: Garrett
text: Awesome food, great atmosphere. Did I mention the food was amazing?

name: Laurie Jenkins
text:
Great for both casual lunch and fancy dinner! I had catered lunch from here, and the sandwiches on fresh homemade foccacia not only looked devine, they tasted amazing as well- very impressive. The catered lunch also came with delicious salads, chips, and ricotta cookies that were omg out of this world delicious!

As far as my dinner experience, their beer and wine selection is reasonable and features local brews. The food was incredible. I had the shrimp fettuccine and it was one of the more balanced in flavor meals I've had. So tasty! My date had the carbonara, and that was scrumptious as well. I would definitely come here again,  but make a reservation- it's not a large space!

resp.text: Thanks so much for the great review.  We love to make great food and making people happy!  Hope you can join us again soon!

name: Wayne Walker
text: Great food and service!

name: Orion Kubat
text: Excellent wine and delicious pastas. Service is professional quality.

name: Caleb Salusso
text: Great Italian restaurant!  Spaghetti and meatballs is my favourite!

name: Leif Wickland
text: Delicious food. Epic desert. Don't miss the tiramisu. Inside tends to be a bit noisy, but the opportunity to sit creekside outside makes up for it. Please do yourself a favor and visit this lovely local spot and eschew the chain places in town.

name: Tristin Fleetwood
text: My favorite restaurant in Bozeman! Their paninis are wonderful! Friendly staff and a great atmosphere!

name: Kevin Hansen
text: Big Timber lamb is awesome

name: Rebecca Belou
text: Have lunch on the patio!  We have had spotty dinner service, but the food is always good.

name: Spencer Cornish
text: Great food, great atmosphere.

name: Ken Olson
text: Great food and service

name: Jim Eischeid
text: Top notch place.

name: Brad Daniel
text: Very nice spot to get lunch!

name: Rose Heider
text: Amazing food and service. Loud atmosphere.

name: Jack Scherman
text: Great environment, equally excellent for both lunch and dinner.  Very friendly staff

name: Alina Karimova
text: The most awesome,  cozy place in Bozeman!

name: jeff kenney
text: Great food and service

name: Brennan Kilty
text: Awesome atmosphere and good food

resp.text: Thanks, Brennan!

name: Toni Brandt
text: Great pasta

name: Paul Fuchs
text: Nice place, good food!

name: Ariel Gobble
text: Amazing food.

resp.text: Thanks!  We are happy you enjoyed it and look forward to seeing you again soon!

name: Tyler Carneal
text: Excellent!

name: JOHN HOLTE
text: Great itialian food

name: Meghan Hertel
text: Dark and relaxed environment

name: Kathy Randle
text: Awesome!!!!

name: Jackson Cyr
text: I like this place

resp.text: Thanks, Jackson.  We are glad you like it here!

name: Colin Pittendrigh
text: Good Italian food

name: Zac Collins
text: Best Lamb Burger ever!!

name: Shonna Grinn
text: Great menu and wine.

resp.text:
Thanks, Jacob!
Hope to see you again!
Thanks for the great photos, Scott.  Hope to see you again soon.

name: Billy Danford
text: Bridger bowl was so beautiful and breathtaking. It was such an easy drive from bozeman. If your looking for a fun and family friendly experience that is affordable for all i definitely recommend bridger bowl. Me and my family had such a wonderful time.

name: William Jakle
text:
Bridger Bowl is literally the only one that's doing reservations and it's pretty much pointless. I would recommend going up to Showdown (an hour up the road).
I've been trying to make reservations ever since they opened and can never get in.. also they make you buy a pass for $5 just so you can buy a lift ticket..
Showdown is also a lot cheaper by at least $15-$20..
I'm at least going to have some fun on the one day off I get...
Peace out Bridger..

name: Bryan Hughes
text: Great mountain with lots of amazing terrain for everyone. The best thing is that their handling of Covid is solid and generally have felt very safe. Their reservation system and limiting of capacity is spot on. Unlike Big Sky which was a super spreader nightmare.

name: Diane Reese Leach
text: Long runs, perfect snowfall, nice staff, very nice restaurants & bars.  Ski shop is well appointed.

name: Cousin Kyle
text: I look forward all year to being able to snowboard the cold smoke

name: Ryan Schwab
text: Dec 1, 2020. Plenty of great snow if you're willing to hike for it!  Probably needs another good storm or two before most of the mountain has proper coverage and they start running the lifts

name: Bill Hanson
text: The best for us locals, especially if retired and go during the week. I really love this place. Another good yet of snow. Nice people operating the lifts and  eateries. Most weekdays the place belongs to you, with wide open runs and only a scattering of skiers and boarders. I’ll be skiing here as long as I am able.

name: Tony Geiser
text: Learned to ski there, it was great to get back there 20 years later. Fantastic mountain from green to double black!

name: Shawn Bates
text: A very nice locals ski resort.  Not as big and fancy as Big Sky but close to town and has some of the best snow around. It can get a bit cold in the middle of winter.  Very normal to have ski temps in the negative. So make sure your skin is all covered and throw and extra layer on.

name: Winter Blackmore
text: Best local ski resort. I grew up skiing here. The staff is friendly and care more about the skiers than making $. The mountain is well cared for with runs for every level. The food is amazing but to save $ we do pack our lunch mostly. They are always improving. Now I'm teaching my kids here and the bunny hill is wonderful. 2 magic carpets and a short lift. Great terrain for the kids to learn to ski on.

name: josiah rodda
text: Of the three major resorts within 2 hours. (Big sky, red lodge and bridger bowl), Bridger is the best resort. Less rocks overall means you need less coverage to have a good experience. If you live in billings it's only 40 more min more than red lodge for a bigger resort. Least expensive of the 3. No holiday rates. Good restaurant at the lodge.

name: Chris Schmandt
text: It was summer and I went to hike not to ski. The route to the top is not well marked so it's good to have a map but you get up to the ridge rather quickly. In the early summer the flowers are beautiful

name: Ty Walsh
text: Great local spot with a variety of terrain at an affordable price.

name: Doug O'Brien
text: Looks fun. Easy parking close by.

name: Drake Pannell
text: Would've given 5 stars if open in the summer.

name: James Weston Eckhardt
text: I want to give it one star so it nevers shows up in searches and it can stay a secret... but what the heck. It's just the best, simply put. Affordable, local, tons of fun.

name: Tyler Cote
text: Awesome place to ski. Awesome variety of terrain from beginner to experts. Excellent snow conditions. Employees are good natured and actually appear to enjoy working at this awesome little mountain. Parking, lifts, lodges are all top notch and the price is right! Also, the staff was super helpful helping us plan a ski and stay package. Great customer service!

name: Rich Winget
text: Best ski area Gallatin County.

name: Mark Bruschwein
text: Awesome spot with all levels of terrain.

name: Katy K
text:
I liked this park because of the greens. There are a few greens great for beginners. That's me.

There are several blues next to Green's as you come down i end my 9 year old got on a blue by accident.  Ugh. Horrible.  But we stayed strong and eventually made it down.

If following correctly (which i didn't) from the top can go a long way on greens to bottom.  The best way to get better is to practice and ski.  This park can allow that for new skiers.

2 places to get rental skis.  At lodge and  about 100 feet below lodge.  There is a convenience at the lodge when leaving closer, right there to check in.  The other rental place, you have a bit of a hike down to return the skis.

Note we used the one further down not at the lodgr. Great service! Fast and they checked our gear right there. Nice place.

name: Jessica Camp
text: I'm from Massachusetts and had never been skiing before but your instructors were amazing and patient. Lines weren't long. Beautiful snow!

name: Andrew Commander
text: The powder is too deep

name: Sean Smith
text: We visit with a group of college friends at least once a year. This is an excellent ski area with awesome snow and variety of terrain at an affordable price. The lift belts make the lines go quickly too!

name: Julie Dobbins
text: Friendly staff. Love the simple, hometown feel. Bridger is a non-profit, so the prices are reasonable and my kids have had such great learning experiences in they ski school!

name: Nicole Masters
text: Great friendly staff. Nice open slopes without crowds or waiting for lifts.  Awesome day.

name: will it can it should I
text: Awesome, awesome and more awesome plus plenty of powder to go around.

name: T.W. Winston
text: Came to visit friends in Bozeman and brought our gear. This mountain is best suited for skiers, but we snowboarded.  Unreal steep chutes. Bring your av beacon cause you can't access parts of the mtn w/o it.  Had fun as snowboarders just gotta plan your way out. Lots of flat sections on bottom. Snowed everyday we were here.

name: Akyra Moto
text: Great place to walk and hike in the summer.

name: Jack Fry
text: Bridger is a fantastic mountain! There is a large variety in terrain across the mountain, along with good snow coverage most of the time. The staff is very friendly, and the community among skiers and snowboarders is very strong here. Food at the lodges is very good, although there can be a lack of seating on busy days. The wait for lift lines usually isn't very long, at least on the upper mountain, and the scenery is extremely beautiful.

name: Ethan Bowen
text: Great local mountain with amazing runs. With diverse runs ranging from novice greens to technical ridge lines, Bridger Bowl stands out as a pristine MT mountain.

name: Michael Macmanus
text: This is the local spot vs the corporate resort down south. The vibes and price points are the best in the state.

name: Ron Dorey
text: Good prices - skiing terrain is either very advanced or beginner to mild intermediate - not much in between.  Less commercialization here than most hills.

name: David Bouchat
text: Great ski and only 30 minutes from town.

name: Jamie Severson
text: Great skiing! I've skiid here since I was 5 (22 now) and I always find new places to explore. If you eat at any of the Lodges, you must try the fries! 🍟

name: Andy Doughty
text: Great local ski hill with plenty of back-country access and great terrain.

name: Dave and Reine Broome
text: Bozeman’s very own ski area. Located just 25 min from downtown Bridger Bowl has terrain you satisfy everyone from beginners to experts.

name: Joshua Francis
text: Wonderful local ski area.

name: Torin Pfundt
text: Awesome small town feel, with some pretty gnarly terrain.

name: Corey LeBlanc
text: It's our local hill. We love skiing it as a family. I would ski this place even if I didnt live nearby.

name: Geoff Dowell
text: Class trip ski day. Everyone had a great time. Ski staff was amazing and helpful for all.

name: Official Alaskan
text: I understand with a growing concern for health and safety that the mountain was closed down early however that does not excuse the fact that it was only open for 3 hours and I paid for a full price ticket ($63). Regardless of how you look at it this is theft from every single person (that bought a day ticket) that went up on the 15th only to have it closed at noon. We were not told at the ticket office that the mountain would be closing down at noon either.

name: Fimm Blemfskey
text: Very nice 👌

name: Austin Baldwin
text: Best Hometown Skiing Around!

name: Mark Simmons
text: People and slopes are fantastic. Love to see a nicer, more ski-lodge worthy restaurant/lounge area.

name: JuicyH2O
text: Definitely going to be a different kind of review here. Absolutely I totally to phenomenal place to go. Has Great Hills ski starting from kid areas to the most extreme Peak areas. Usually a very busy area but if you go towards the top of the hill most people aren't there yet and it's best to go in the trees where you can find fresh powder all ways. They have secret little hideouts you can always go to which makes the mountain always more fun. Restaurants they're absolutely amazing as the food is always cooked fresh at least every 30 minutes. Have a great variety of foods such as Pizza chili other soups Burgers hot dogs and others. The seating is always great and usually recommend sitting outside so you can enjoy the Sun and eat your fresh amazing fries. Definitely a great place to go for a family event and enjoy good slopes. Prices are pretty good but exactly what you should expect.

name: _ josh kinzle
text: I'm a big fan of bridger bowl

name: Eric Sterkel
text: Great local ski area.  If you want strep and deep then this is it! Runs are short lines are short so laps are easy. Lessons for kids are fantastic!

name: Joe Polasik
text: Get family ski area

name: Brian McCurdy
text: Great family mountain, that also happens to have amazing adult-only terrain...

name: Eli Anselmi
text: Great skiing, no lines to small lines, where locals go, tons of snow and great runs.

name: Siwa Links
text: I thoroughly enjoyed the lush amount of absorbent and floofy snow. In fact, it was the finest grains of snow flecks that I have ever had the pleasure of witnessing. I mean, I would have stripped down naked and pleasured my self in those beautiful snow fluffs had they let me.

name: Mike Hickert
text: Bridger is best! A lot has changed -  mostly for the good - since the 90's when I first went to Bridger but you can tell all the growth around the valley when on a normal day the parking lot is filled up. Still not anywhere near as bad as the big Cali and Colorado resorts and a lift ticket is half as much as Big Sky.

name: Jenny Trottier
text: I love this place! So absolutely beautiful❤

name: Dave Johnston
text:
Great local ski hill.

Not enough can be said about how awesome the entire staff is!

name: Jon Hodge
text: Not worth visiting no gondolas stay away

name: David Relph
text: Best place to go skiing in the area with a bunch of locals and college students. If you are looking for a ski resort however I would advise Big Ski. Bridger has one main lodge at the bottom with two smaller ones on the mountain. The skiing is great for the price but hands down looses to Big Sky in amenities. All in all if you're looking to ski all day and not care about the lifts or lodges go to Bridger. If you want a really nice ski resort go to Big Sky and stop complaining about our little old ski area in the national forest.

name: Bryan Rask
text: Go Jimbo!!! Can’t wait to get married here this coming fall!!

name: Mi W
text:
Had so much fun but the staff on the
Lifts were  rude and unpleasant

name: Sheldon Young
text: They need to have HIGH SPEED quad lifts. Don't really appreciate spending all my time on a lift... Big sky has much faster lift for 60 dollars more... Also as well you don't have to spend your day switching lifts. I spent all day switching lifts and wish there was just one lift that went all the way to the top so I don't have to get off one lift, then ski for 100 yards then get on another lift to go all the way to the top. I wish I could remember this place as a great ski area not a day where I spent my day on lifts...

name: Tiffany Cok
text: Our family loves skiing Bridger Bowl.

name: jake orhai
text: A down home ski hill, even as it grows. Some of the best days of my life were spent skipping school as a kid to come play up there. Still home to kids skipping school, whole families skipping responsibilities, dirtbags who never had any responsibilities to begin with, as well as a grip of world class rippers, increasingly wealthier college kids, and every other social strata from the valley and Livingston. The terrain speaks for itself.

name: Jack Habenicht
text: Great for early season hiking and boarding.

name: Gregg Fuller
text: Dave the head of ski school is an arrogant jerk. It's time for somebody else to replace him. I've had nothing but poor experiences with a very few handful of the staff. The lift operators are a different sort of character. They are always happy and smiling and a joy to be around.

name: James Willich
text: Tons of fun. Good variety.

name: Landon Becnel
text: Easily the best ski area for the money (but don't tell anyone).

name: Chris Moseman
text: Fun and affordable. I experienced some great snow for the 2017/2018 season. Only complaints is that it gets really busy, parking can be very difficult and include a long walk to the lift. Lifts lines aren’t too horrible, but the snow gets tracked out fast. Still had some amazing days there and learned to snowboard moguls like a pro.

name: Aidan Andersen
text: Amazing ski runs, amazing staff. A must see for everyone who loves sking/snowboarding

name: Damir Davis
text: Not too expensive, the vibe is great and the runs are fast. Lifts are a little long. Looking for fresh runs might be challenging.

name: Tom Mason
text: Great staff! Really good lessons. Rental staff are very helpful. Buildings are clean and well organized. Great selection of various skill level runs.

name: Aaron Pursell
text: Fantastic ski area, staff is super friendly and helpful. Lifts are super nice with conveyors. Tables can be a problem because people are jerks and can't read and leave their stuff on tables even though they're not supposed to. Staff could enforce it...but doesn't. Just move people's stuff to the floor...

name: Micheal McCuen
text: A major ski resort. We thoroughly enjoyed the courteous helpful staff and other skiers. Rate equal with Big Sky and better value

name: Cameron Waters
text: Picked up season passes and visited the Raptor Festival! Snow can't come soon enough! 🤓💕🎿🌨️❄️☃️🌡️🤓

name: Only Nate
text: A fantastic local ski area that serves up cold smoke. It can be packed on the weekends, but it’s a best price ski area. The whole area is great and can meet the needs of all skiers.

name: Allison Miles
text: Wonderful community ski hill! The french fries make even the coldest days great!

name: John Caldwell
text: One of the best local ski areas in the country. No one will be disappointed!

name: Pete Wenzel
text: Great service and the mountain is beautiful.

name: Sean Kretovics
text: Awesome place to ski, never too crowded. Can't go wrong with a day at Bridger!

name: Sean McSherry
text: Great skiing at a great price. Great for skiing on a budget.

name: Brannin McBee
text: The best local ski hill

name: Jude
text: Clever folks know to drive north to Bridger and stay away from Big Sky.

name: Jen Woodward
text: This is a beautiful drive during the early spring early summer days.  I’ve never skied here I’ve only driven to Bozeman and back through.  I love the drive!  However, If you have any motion sickness people with you this might not be the way to go!

name: Elif Bilal
text: Staff members were extremely helpful on my very first day snowboarding as I fell down several hundred times.

name: Mark Woodard
text: Great skiing for all ages and abilities

name: Sukhyung Shin
text: Loved the steeps on the left side of the map.  Chairlifts are mostly triples and cover a ton of terrain.

name: Kevin Barland
text: Spent 3 days at this mountain last week.  Great fun mountain to ride, locals were cool AF.  Not much of a nightlife, but you're close enough to Bozeman you can cruise there if you want.  Not too expensive to ski either.  Rented a cabin that we could ski to, so that was a cool experience.

name: Brian Norlin
text: Great snow, great lodge, great staff!

name: M Kirk
text: Great place to ski and family friendly! Season passes are very reasonable, especially for young children!

name: Sea Jae Cocalope
text: The mountain itself was good, it was their policy and one particular employee who earned this review. I went up to buy my ticket and asked if they have a military discount. The lady said for active military, which I asked what about for veterans? And she replied with such astonishing rudeness when she explained that unless I had proof of still being active, she’d never approve such a discount, and it wasn’t only the wording, it was her tone of unusual disgust that left my jaw on the floor, as well as all of the people around me. Following the conversation, there was my brother and I, and about 12 other people talking about her and how she handled that, everyone being extremely taken back. An older couple offered to pay my ticket, but I explained to them that it wasn’t about the money, it’s the principle of the matter. Now had she been polite about it, like every human being should be, then I would’ve given three stars, as I feel our military members, ESPECIALLY ones who have spent years away from home fighting a war for our damn country, should be given a discount, and it was her rude dimeanor that brought this down to one star. Unless something changes, I will take my business to big sky where they honor our military for the remainder of my time in Bozeman. Thank you.

resp.text: Hello Sea, Thank you for your feedback on your recent visit to Bridger Bowl. I apologize that you had an unfortunate customer service experience. Our goal is for visitors to have the best experience and due to your review we can take the opportunity to improve our staff interactions and overall visitor experience. As a non-profit, community ski area our mission is to keep skiing affordable for everyone. We do offer a discount for Active Military. Thank you for your service and time. Cheers

name: Floyd Morris
text: This place is amazing.   Great snow, small lift lines,  even on a holiday!

name: Steven Atkin
text: Might be some of the best in the lower 48

name: caleb hart
text: Great family friendly place. Great people, including other skiers

name: Douglas Crumpler
text: Very busy, extensive parking and great snow skiing. Food good but expensive.

name: Joseph Bernhardt
text: There's just something about this place.  It doesn't matter that the wind is blowing twenty miles per hour or that there are fifteen minute lines for the lift.  This place is a community.  It has a warmth, a kindness, that makes it feel like home.

name: Steven Shope
text: The place just sucks, stay away, Big Sky is a much better hill to ski on.

name: Sandra Kennedy Moore
text: Okay, not great.  Good selection of food.  Okay Blues. I agree with the famous sticker, "Who cares if you skied Bridger."

name: Jack Scherman
text: This locally owned ski hill is a great place with diverse terrain and reasonable prices.  Loved by the locals for a good reason, Bridger is located in a beautiful canyon close to Bozeman. Not crowded on weekdays

name: Nick Stark
text: I got a season pass here for $350 because I was 18 at the time, even though it's no where near as large as other resorts I'd rather spend the entire season here. The two new lifts are great as well. I always have and always will love Bridger Bowl more than any other "big" surrounding resort

name: Doug Coombs
text: Best F&B manager in the business!

name: Brock Jimerson
text: Amazing mountain. Great ridge line to hike. And hit it the right day you want be sorry

name: David Bruce
text: The lodge updates are nice.

name: Andy Amidon
text: Great runs, big snow, affordable and family friendly....no need to go outside Bozeman

name: Monkey Belle
text: There are tons of good runs

name: Brennon Moor
text: Absolutely amazing skiing at a price that isn't going to break the bank. Super friendly staff and great people. Honestly my favorite ski area in Montana.

name: putzmarie
text: Had a really good day of snowboarding with really nice powder.

name: Daniel Swanson
text:
I’m a bit bummed out because we ended last year with a few hundred dollars left worth of credit at the kids club and they said it would transfer to this year, but now they won’t honor it.  Really lame.
That being said- PK is probably my favorite lift in the world.
This place can get crowded but if you are down to work a bit for your lines... best skiing in the world.
Just kinda bummed about their customer service.

name: T. Clint Stone
text: We always have a blast at Bridger! Tons of runs from beginner to expert laid out on the face of a huge Montana mountain, get there early so you have time to hit all the lifts, there's a lot to see and do!

name: JEFF FLAMMANG
text: This is a great place for the family.  Ski lessons for ten weeks cost $220 and well worth it.  I have two kids in them right now.

name: Zach Purdy
text: Lots of diversity. Extremely fair priced. You can't have a bad time here.

name: Janet Jones
text: A Beautiful Sunny Ski Day

name: Vincent Stephan
text: Love you Bridger bowl! Hope climate change doesn't make you extinct

name: Liz Biehl
text: I had such a fun time at Bridger Bowl today with my son at his school trip there!! I haven't skied myself for 30-sone years and e eery one was great at helping! My son and I loved it!!

name: Deborah Causey
text: Did some hiking and enjoyed the beautiful day.

name: Kirkwood Donavin
text: This is the local spot, beloved by many. It's very close to Bozeman and offers a full range of terrain, including allowing experts to hike the Ridge for some excellent "side-country". It's not a destination resort and that's probably for a few reasons: short runs and crowded weekend lift lines; There are no hi-speed chair lifts. But, I'll continue to love this place as long as I live in Bozeman.

name: Sean McCleary
text:
I grew up Skiing here and still continue to go. I have skied at other areas and they don't have the same laid back attitude of Bridger. This area has expanded a lot and offers many options for skiers of all abilities.

Price has gradually climbed over the years. Half day is not half price! Full day is $60 and half day is $51 so don't go up there late with the assumption of a screaming deal.

name: Laura Askew
text: Loved that it doesn’t feel like a resort.

name: Jackson Riepe
text: Great community resort- always a good time!!

name: Jeff Langford
text: Awesome place to ski

name: Taylor Lonsdale
text: Simply the best in SW Montana

name: Austin Brauer
text: At only 15 minutes or of Bozeman with no traffic, it's hard to beat Bridger Bowl. Has a great range of terrain from beginner green circles to shoot drops that will make Legolas's shield surfing look easy! Plus the food is pretty dang good. It's rather steep, but I get the chilly cheese fries for 8 bucks and usually can't finish. Don't waste your time and money on a trip to Bigsky this year just stay close to home and shred on the cold smoke!

name: jennifer leigh
text: Wasnt here to ski. Came for a horseback poker ride with Gallatin Valley Backcountry Horsemen riding club. It was awesome.

name: Terrell Porter
text: Shhhhh, wonderful, friendly local unknown snow sports area. Keep the secret, the staff is great.

name: Mark C
text: The only thing that really needs improvement is the labeling of the trails. Otherwise great all around!

name: kai hogen
text: Best local mountain! Great terrain with it resort bells and whistles.. Super kids program!

name: Karl Baer
text: One of the last public non profit ski areas in the world.  An amazing mountain for families.

name: Linda Hogg
text: Loved skiing the Cold Smoke today!

name: Les Craig
text: No greater place to teach children to ski from age 3 to double black diamond (shortly thereafter)!

name: Eamonn McCoy
text: Fun resort, good snow. Best place is the ridge by far

name: C W Wines
text: Probably the best community owned ski area in the country.  Not impressed with grooming this year.

name: Leif Wickland
text: Sure. I'd like faster lifts. Sure I'd like more convenient parking. But you really can't beat Bridger's convenience or value.

name: steven sullivan
text: Plenty of snow, no lift lines and some great terrain during our trip.

name: Natasha Shaty
text: Even on the busiest days, there's plenty of open room and space for everyone.

name: John Everett
text: a GREAT PLACE TO SKI   No Glamour or glitz . Just Great Skiing

name: Michael Jakubic
text: Very fun! Don't go too high up in the mountain if you don't think you can get down, there is some steep terrain.

name: William O'Neill
text: Always awesome to be here. I love this mountain.

name: Dave Keating
text: We were involved in the remodel and it looks great I will be back to ski and say hi to the owner what a nice guy.

name: Rusty Squire
text: Some of the best side country of any US ski resort but for the average skier they don't groom nearly enough terrain, especially off the Bridger Lift. I'm there for the former and not the latter but as I age I may find myself back at Big Sky.

text:
We have adopted 3 pets here and recently had my son's birthday party here. The kids had a lot of fun at a very reasonable price for the number of guests you can bring.

This is a no kill shelter, and they have very passionate people who work there and volunteers who give their free time to help the animals.

If you are ever considering getting a pet, please adopt here instead of buying dogs from puppy mills or classified ads. You will find a friend for life, while helping save many other friends with your support.

One place that deserves more than 5 stars.

name: iridescent55
text: This is a wonderful animal rescue group and facility, staffed by caring, compassionate, and lovely people. I did see some animals that could have used some more medical and dental attention, but overall the animals appear to be well-taken care of. The facility is kind of out in the middle of the boonies, and I can see several advantages to that location. They have fantastic dog runs and areas open for public use. Heart of the Valley makes adoption easy, and it is apparent that adopting the critters to loving forever homes is priority. It is also extra fantastic that they are open every day of the week, accommodating most every schedule. Thanks HotV, keep up the good work!

text: Awesome animal shelter! The staff is friendly and they have nice walking trails and various fenced areas for dogs. Off leash areas for group and individual use pens. One of them is full of agility equipment. They provide a great service to the community and in turn they receive a lot of community support.

I don't know how they do it, but they recommended a 4 month old cat as a mouser and I adopted her for my partner's family, now she is honestly a mouse killing machine. Which sounds kinda gross but that's the way cats are. I have primarily volunteered in the cat room and the staff are so loving and compassionate. Everything is really organized and professional too.

name: Dave Johnston
text:
Employees are kind, about half of them can help you find something in the store, and there are a small few you could ask for expert advice, but let's face it: one does not go to a Home Depot to learn how to do complicated home repairs from an employee there.

I mean, I love Wal-Mart and shop there all the time, but I wouldn't go to Wal-Mart looking for fashion advice or tips on how to decorate my home.

If you want expert advice or specialized parts, go to Owenhouse.

If you need supplies they don't carry at the hardware store, if you're a do it yourself kind of person, the project isn't too big, and you need lumber or generic hardware, plumbing or electrical supplies, it's great to have a Home Depot (and the store across the street) in town.

And, as I've said, while not everyone there will send you in the right direction for what you're looking for, the people there are very nice.

I don't know if it's just a local problem or nationwide, but they really need to do their stocking at night like most other stores, not during shopping hours. The ability to access the aisles and the ability to shop in the store is very important, and is so hampered by products, boxes, ladders, and carts that it is not worth the frustration and extra time to shop at Home Depot. text:
They are absolutely lost.  I ordered a camera (nest) over 3 weeks ago in their store... there was no delay charging my bank account... then they said the camera was not in the store.  Customer service said there were 7 of those cameras coming in two days later and they would pull one and call me... waited 12 days, no calls, nothing.  Went into the store and talked to customer service... person tried to give me someone else's merchandise (fortunate for them, I'm honest).  The cameras came in and were "in a box somewhere", after which I was advised the prior "trained to open the boxes" do not work weekends, so I would have to wait one day and they would call me... three days later, no calls.  Got passed around on the phone and last person said they couldn't find them, but they would call me (yeah, sure.).  Went to the store and talked to customer service who said they didn't know which box the cameras were in... spoke with manager (Kiara Linschied) who said she was going to get with electrical team and find them "today" (this was in the morning) and she would personally call me back.  Well, a day has passed--no calls, nothing.  I called today (she gave me her card) and it went to her extension and the fellow who answered told me "she's off today"... lol, no surprise.  I gave him my info and he said he would look and call me back.... not holding my breath.  I'll shop Lowes from this day forward--they lost me.

Recommend steering clear of Home Depot for any in-store out of stock orders... they don't care about you as a customer at all--you're not relevant, so just know that when you do business with them.

text:
We were very excited to go to the Bay tonight for dinner. We have been once before and the food and service was excellent. Unfortunately we cannot say the same tonight. The service was slow and just didn't seem to really be there. I asked for a straw for my drink at least 3 times. Then when our orders came out, the huckleberry burger was not cooked as asked and they forgot the sauce (huckleberry bbqs buger). We asked and got some on the side. My order had a HAIR wrapped around it! When the server asked how our food was I told him about the hair, and he just replied "okay". So the hair sat there while I ate the rest of my food. Then a man came out in a button up shirt, I think the manager he didn't introduce himself, and asked how things were and we told him about the hair, he took it with the piece of food and never returned.
Our waiter offered us a dessert to make it right and so we said yes. It was very good dessert. But our 3 year old sons kids meal came with a sundae, and we asked for it when we got our dessert, the waiter said he would go grab it. Then next time he came out he brought us the check and no Sundae. So we just skipped it rather than wait around for it again.
The food, other than the undercooked burger, and the hair in the other meal. It all tasted good. The calamari state was horrible, better last time we visited. And well, definitely not good service. For the price, I dont think we will ever be back.

text:
We've stopped by The Bay several times, over the years, when we pass through Bozeman.  Yesterday, on our way home, we realized it had been awhile, so we decided to swing in for late lunch / early dinner.  Turned out to be a good call.

We arrived around 4pm.  We were greeted & seated immediately.  We were the first table to be seated in the Dining Room.  Our server, Jillian, stopped in several times to check on us, as we settled in.  It took us around 20 minutes to actually get to the point of placing our food order.  Jillian was patient & very helpful with suggestions & recommendations.

Since it was Happy Hour, we opted to get some apps & a drink.  Here's the run down:

I ordered a Moscow Mule & The Wife ordered a Strawberry Martini.  Both drinks were very tasty & presented well.

Shrimp Wontons:  Crispy, nice temp on arrival, lots of cream cheese, decent amount of shrimp.  Both sauces were great.  Overall these were really good.

Chicken Sliders:  Awesome app!  There's a ton of flavor packed into these little cluckers.  The texture was perfect & the chicken was moist.
Home Run!

House Made Chips & Onion Dip:  Mixture of potato & beet chips.  Chips were just a smidge over cooked.  Not much, but just.  We all liked them & the Onion Dip was quite good.  Little Guy really liked these chips.
Dragon Tenders:  We got 1/2 Buffalo & 1/2 Dragon.  The chicken was cooked well, both sauces were great.  Wife said Buffalo won, but I'm on Team Dragon.  The Ranch & Blue Cheese which accompanied the tenders were both top notch.  Probably the best Blue Cheese I've had, at this level of restaurant.

Little Guy opted for the Cheese Pizza from the Kid's Menu.  He loved it!  This kid knows his Pizza, so take notice.  Kid's meal comes with an Ice Cream Sundae, which he enjoyed as well.

The Space:  I wish I had better news here.  The Dining Room is in need of an immediate update.  The tables are very worn, the carpet (yes carpet), in the Dining Room is tired & homely & the driftwood on the ceiling, of the Dining Room, is just nasty looking.  Wife said the Ladies restroom needed a custodial visit.  The better news is this:  None of these things equate to what's on the plate.  However, they still should be addressed.

Service:  I'm just gonna say it, Jillian has been the best server we've had in Montana, in at least a year or two.  She was on top of her game & we noticed.  A+  If you appreciate a Veteran Server, who knows how it's done, ask to be seated in her area.  I almost forgot to mention, the Manager also stopped by our table to ask how everything was.  Well done!

4.0 Star Review

text:
Absolutely amazing! Saffron Table was recommended by several people that I met while working a wellness event and I am so glad that they did! They told us to make a reservation as it is a super small spot that fills up fast most days of the week and I am so glad they did that as well! The food is out of this world good! My friend and I ordered their Saffron Table Vegetarian Thali that came with the choice of two curries plus either naan or rice. We picked their aloo gobi, which is roasted cauliflower and potatoes tossed in a tomato sauce with cumin, onion, and chili. And their butter paneer which was a buttery curry with tomato, cream, and lemon juice. Both came with delicious and savory sauces that were oh so good! I loved and wanted to keep eating every bite of them with the light and a hint of sweet garlic naan! I cannot wait to eat my leftovers tomorrow!

Also the service and atmosphere were just amazing as well! The staff make you feel at home and the lighting and decorations just make you want to stay and chill all day eating garlic naan and sipping on wines from their great selection of whites, reds, sparklings, and beers.

Definitely worth a stop or two while in Bozeman!

We ordered the Palak Paneer and the Butter Paneer, both of which were delicious and perfectly seasoned. I also highly recommend the garlic naan which goes well with any dish. The menu is well curated, featuring a wide variety of dishes without overwhelming you with decisions. Many vegetarian and gluten-free options are available as well.

text:

text: We had the lamb and a version of the chicken curry. Everything that we ordered tasted amazing and was presented beautifully! The staff were fantastic as well and had a great atmosphere. Recommend making a reservation however because we did not and had to sit at the bar where the chairs were not comfortable, but it was ok. The desert was fantastic as well!

text:
Extremely authentic, and unique. Spice was a bit more than I was expecting, but quantity was superb and left enough for a second meal, providing you make more rice.

Presentation was very professional, I had the saffron rice, and it was a work of art.

A patty of naan was $4, but was very good.

Seating is scarce, so make sure to have reservations.

name: Kendall Stewart

Naan bread is some of my favorite food and I ordered every kind they had, and I'm glad I did! We really enjoyed our time here and the waitress did such a fantastic job recommending us the perfect dishes! My father loved the beer she suggested SOOO much!

The. Best. Place to eat in Bozeman.

Very good food!

The naan is to die for, they always have a great beer selection and their rotating daily specials are fantastic! If you are looking for a great place to have dinner in Bozeman, with a skilled polite staff, Saffron is an excellent choice!

name: Chrystina Katz

resp.text: Dear Spencer,  We're thrilled to hear that you enjoyed your dinner at Saffron Table. Thank you for kind review. We look forward to seeing you again soon.

text: Really high quality food with incredible flavors. My expectations were high going in, yet they were exceeded with each dish. One of the best meals I've had in Bozeman.

I would have to agree, no use of spices whatsoever and the prices are too high for the quality. The inside is cute but they need dividers - it gets wayyyyyyy too loud in what used to be a house lol.

name: Erica Burrell
text: Always impeccable, the half a dozen times we've been there. The food is the best in Gallatin Valley as far as I am concerned. We lucked out and had our meal in the upper room which was exactly what we needed as we arrived early and enjoyed most of our dinner alone. I have to note the design and ambiance of the room is unique to all of Bozeman. The whole restaurant is inviting but the upper room is superbly designed with soft chairs and a fireplace tucked away, all in a farmhouse bedroom! It is decorated with unique and natural art in an intimate space. It feels exclusive, as it only seats a few couples. It is a bit chilly in the winter without the fireplace lit but the overall experience was divine!

name: Jae Evans
text: The best Indian cuisine around. I took a coworker who lives in India to the Saffron Table and he said it was the best Indian food he's had in the US. If you ask them to make it hot, you better mean it!

name: Montana Review
text:
Overall Rating: Good for what we've got.

It's easy to say that this barbecue is a mockery of Southern barbecue or even Montana made barbecue, but for what it's worth, this food chain does a great job with its quality of food and selection. The meat is always cooked perfectly and deliciously, with great rubs and sauces. The sides are also quite good and you have a good variety of sides and combos plates to choose from. You'll spend as much as you spend on other sit down chain restaurants, which is worth it for a place like this, who actually cares about the food it's serving you.

name: Tim Hart
text:
Roasted chicken with onion strings - oh my goodness - soul food.  Be sure to try the Founders Feast for 2 - you can definitely serve three with this!

Founder's Feast
Famous Dave's favorite meal. Georgia Pork, 1/4 Flame-Kissed or BBQ Chicken, 3 St. Louis-Style Spareribs, Sweet Corn, Wilbur Beans, Creamy Coleslaw, Famous Fries and a Corn Bread Muffin.

resp.text: Holy smokes Tim!!! What a testimony ;) We're beyond thrilled to hear that you enjoyed your Famous Feast with us. P.S. Every Tuesday we offer a special for $10 off every Feast For Two. Hope to see you again soon!

name: Dave Voice of NH
text:
Just stopped along the way between campsites, Yellowstone to Glacier. Famous Dave's was right next to the road and has lots of space to park my rig, along with the dozen or so people who got there before me. The service? Great. The food? Duh, it's Famous Dave's -- always tops. It's a very busy place which says a lot, and lots of local people eat there from what I see (that says a lot about the place).

My only regret: I had a half-rack of ribs, and tried to sample a different BBQ sauce with each rib piece. I ran out of ribs before I tried each one. I should have gotten the full rack.

Truly enjoyable lunch, nice atmosphere, very attentive service. Unqualified five-stars for this one!

text: This was a random find, but happy that I did.  The food was 3.5/5 star, but the great beer selection, the atmosphere, and the friendly staff make up the difference. name: Run-A-Way Bill
text:
Gardiner, Wyoming -

The “Two Bit Saloon” is a local neighborhood bar, year round & a “Run-A-Way Bill” Favorite bar.

The atmosphere, the staff & the local customers are super-riffic!

I cannot remember laughing so much - left with so many “More Smiles Than I Came In With!”.

Bartender Vicky, owner Chuck, and my newest pARTy Pals “Angela”, “Carter” & “Nicholas” made me feel part of their village.

The “Two Bit Saloon” & bartender “Vicky” are both “Run-A-Way Bill” FAVORITE sticker winners.

“Run-A-Way Bill” was here! (& will return)

06.24.19

name: Jamie RK
text: We were standing inside for 10 minutes and no one even acknowledged us. Even just a "hello" or "welcome" would have sufficed. 3 servers/hostesses/workers walked by us and no one said anything. Had it been just my husband and I we wouldn't mind waiting, but we were also with our parents, one being my father in law who has COPD and was recently diagnosed with cancer. He's also a veteran. Having him wait like this wasn't fair so we left. Can't say anything about their food, unfortunately we could not get past their service.

text: I only came for the food and i loved the drinks. The bartender mad us a Happy Fun it was somewhere in the Pina Colad flavor area lol and the other was a homewrecker which was crown,grape pucker and well I can't remember the rest lol. We ordered a cheeseburger and fries fyi so dang yummy and the fries are so golden and hot and mmmmm. It is now another favorite burger spot of mine in Gardiner. Looking around the room everyone who was eating there had pretty much cleaned there plates and seemed to have left happy about there meal. I know i was very pleased with my meal and enjoyed it all.

name: Jaime Decker
text:
We went there Saturday (August 1st) and stood in the hallway next to the entrance. After about 5 minutes and no hello, or how can we help you, I went inside and asked if they were only doing take out? Or could we stay to eat? I was told the other room had plenty of tables or that we could sit outside. I told the young lady that we would be happy to have a table in the next room and that as long as it was ok with her we would go wait for her there. We sat ourselves and waited for approximately 15 minutes with no interaction whatsoever from the staff. No water, 'i' ll be right with you '... Nothing. So we left and went to the sushi place next door.
The only reason there are 3 stars and not zero is that I've eaten here quite a bit before and it was awesome. The menu seems to have changed (I don't know if it's because of covid or just a menu change) but I was sad that my favorites were no longer on the menu either.
You asked so here is my novel of a story. Thanks for caring enough to ask

resp.text: Hey Jaime, We are so sorry this happened. We'll be sending this to our GM to make sure in the future this doesn't repeat itself!

text: Nice food, I'm a fan, pretty calm environment.

resp.text: Thanks for the positive review Sage! Any way we can improve to make it a full 5 stars next time?

name: Jana Cichowski
text: Great place but it's small. Beautiful food served quick and with style. Everything here is gluten free. I haven't eaten fried foods in a decade. What a treat!

resp.text: Thanks Jana! That is so great to hear. (and stay tuned as we are working on expanding our seating.)

name: Emily Lawrence
text: I have been to Lot G many times and generally love their food. However the last two times I have gone my food has been burnt. Today my potatoes were completely burnt on the outside and raw on the inside and my friend's little Danish pancakes were black on the outside. The chicken fried steak and eggs were good, so was the coffee and service otherwise. Hopefully they fix it as I love the place!

resp.text: Hi Emily, I am so sorry to hear that! It must have been incredibly disappointing, especially when you've enjoyed our food in the past. It is of course not our goal to serve burned food and it's good to hear about it so we can fix the problem. We've been training some new staff and I will pass this on to our manager so she can make sure that everyone is getting the same instructions about how we want our food to be prepared. I'm hopeful that your next visit will prove that we can still serve up the great food you expect and deserve.

name: Lindsey Rue Marrow
text: Absolutely adore this place! My girlfriends and I love to go have brunch there. The service and food are exceptional. The owner is one of the kindest ladies I’ve ever had the pleasure of knowing. It’s no wonder her staff is so wonderful! Highly recommend their specials and the chicken and grits with sausage gravy.

resp.text: Hooray! That is so nice to hear Lindsey! We love hearing that we're a preferred brunch spot. And you're right - our owner is a wonderful person who attracts other great people to her! We really appreciate your taking the time leave a review for us (and our other sister businesses) and we look forward to hosting you for another ladies' brunch soon!

name: Brian Rauch
text: This is a unique menu, and offers a full range of gluten free dishes. There is two seating areas, and the food came quickly. I wouldn't recommend this for a place to bring kids due to it's more adult focused menu. There is plenty of parking, but not in front of the actual building. But much easier than a down town location!

resp.text: Hello Brian, thank you so much for taking the time to leave such a nice and comprehensive review - that is so helpful for future diners and we really like being able to hear what you liked or didn't like about your visit! We hope to see you again soon.
