text: It is worth every penny. The steaks we had were cooked to perfection. The sides were just as  large as the entrees and divine. Swiss chard, mac n cheese and carrots were some of our groups sides and they were all shareable.  It was expensive but a must try.

resp.text: Wow - thank you!  Cheers!

name: Mark Allen
text: Best steaks I've had in 4 years in Bozeman. Servers are knowledgeable and attentive, bartenders are beyond phenomenal, and the back of house staff obviously know what they're doing. Plus they have Don Julio 1942 for 26 dollars for a single shot, can't beat that!

resp.text: Wow - thank you for the kind words.  Cheers!

name: FENGYAN ZHANG
text: Best steak in Bozeman. Bothe ribeye and New York were cooked perfectly. Don’t miss the cream brûlée.

resp.text: Thank you for your review and the kind words.  Cheers!

name: Nathan Knopf
text:
We used to eat here regularly and bring clients with us. I rated them 5 star in the past.  However, they recently changed the menu (which is fine in concept) but not in a good direction this time. All the good selections we like were removed. Even basic salads were not interesting.  We gave up on higher priced menu items and ordered a burger to share.  Also a mistake.  The bun was too thick and very dry. The fries were old and dry tasting.  I give them one star only as it is a nice place because were were provided a sample of a great tasting drink by Matt.  Thank you Matt. You were terrific! We'll come back again after the menu looks interesting again.

Update. Some friends invited us to Open Range. Reluctantly we went tonight 12/2/20. All 6 of us were disappointed.  The food was bland or in other cases way over salted. The new chef is trying to create a menu they don't have the skill set to cook.

Please bring back the old menu, chef, crew.

text: Good service.  Food is fully price but appropriate for the quality.  I had the best whiskey sour drink I have ever had any place.  Nice ambience.  I am so glad I had dinner there.  This is a restaurant that must be tried.

resp.text: Thank you so very much for the kind words. We are happy to hear that you enjoyed yourself.  Cheers!

Although I was a single diner I was treated nicely.  The restaurant is very large inside.  The menu has many creative dishes and I was pleased they came up with a side of vegetables for me when the veggie of the day was sold out.

name: Matt Peoplis
text:
This is how a great dinner out is supposed to be!
Started with wonderful drinks, my martini rocks was perfectly made with one huge rock to keep the chill.
Duck confit was so good I had to pick it up and chew on the bone. Delicious.
The 22oz tomahawk bison ribeye steak was done perfectly . The waitress recommended medium, it was melt in your mouth tender and just delicious.
Crème brûlée with huckleberry topped it off.
The waitress was right on point with recommendations and service.
We had a very memorable experience.
Can't wait to go back.

name: Richard Murphy
text: We love this place. First timers. Three of us had the meat sampler called the asado for two, also had the wedge salad, the bison tenderloin, cream spinach and corn bread. Our server was excellent her recommendations were spot on. She also suggested excellent wine pairings. Oh and do not forget dessert. Some kind of multi version cream brûlée's or custard for dessert

name: Kelly Jones
text: Not very impressed. The waitress forgot our appetizer, made it sound like salad and soup were included in the entree price, didn't refill our drinks until we caught her (and it wasn't busy.) The person who brought out our food put everything in the wrong spots, and a cast iron pan in front of my seven year old that burnt my hand when I bumped it trying to get it out of the way. The waitress said dessert was on her since she forgot our appetizer, and we ordered ice cream for our daughter and a dessert for us to share, and only our dessert was written off.  Partner's burger was really good he said, but my chicken was only ok- I can get a similar dish that's way better for half the price at Ted's. We won't be returning, we'll stick to our favorites- ale works, midtown tavern, Ted's, Urban kitchen. All cheaper and better quality, with good service.

name: Hannah Schweitzer
text: The atmosphere, food, and drinks are upscale and classy. Yet, the service has a casual, friendly and neighborly treatment. Some of the best food I have ever had and every drink I have had there has out done the last. Although, I have had friends who have had a drink not to their taste and the bar is quick to reconcile that by making a drink to their taste based an flavors and drinks they have enjoyed in the past. Some of the best experiences I have had have been on while meeting new people at this bar.

name: Alisha Yoder Ilic
text: Open Range is likely in the top five nicest restaurants in the Bozeman area. It is also one of the more expensive restaurants in the region. The atmosphere is great (I love the lights they put up in the winter) and the cocktails are very good. We have eaten here several times and the service is usually decent and the food is generally very good. Occasionally, the dishes are hit or miss; this isn't uncommon with game meat, however. Regardless, it is worth a try as it is one of the few places you can get a good cut of local elk and bison (not in burger form!).

resp.text: thank you for the kind words.  Cheers!

name: Mike Giroux
text: Delicious and great service.  No, it is not cheap, but very good and friendly service and everything i have had there has been great tasting and well done.  Had the halibut special tonight and never had a better tasting fish dish.  Last time I had the duck and it was the same thing, best ever duck.   Too bad delicious perfection isn't cheap, but... it isn't.

name: Ellie Knight
text: The food here is great and I like going here for special occasions, but in general I feel like the servers act a little indifferent and too cool for school and it really puts me off. Good food, good cocktails, lacking in atmosphere and friendliness.

name: Taunia Kittler
text: Perfect for a family friendly dinner with style.

resp.text: Taunia - thank you for the kind words.  Cheers!

name: John Bishop
text: Always friendly severing staff, amazingly talented and friendly kitchen if you walk by them, and some of the best cocktails in town from some very enjoyable bartenders. Clean and dressy, but at the same time cozy and relaxed. This is the only place in Bozeman I walk in and see people dressed up for a night out or walking in with blue jeans and neither one seem to get in the way of the other or look out if place.    A must go in Bozeman if you want to have a complete Montana dining experience with a little bit of class.

resp.text: Thank you for the kind words. Our hope was to have a restaurant as you described.  Everyone is welcome.  Cheers!

name: Corey LeBlanc
text: Open Range is one of the nicest places to eat in Montana. We always love our food and the dining experience.  We only eat seafood and fish and its  always fresh!

resp.text: thank you for the kind words.  Cheers!

name: Steffan Anderson
text: Great restaurant with great atmosphere. I believe they over-do the smoke flavor in the ketchup, mashed potatoes for example. Beers only in cans, great knowledgeable bartenders make impressive cocktails. The pork chop is a must, as well as their sweet corn bread as a dessert. Will continue to return.

name: Jae Evans
text: Open Range probably has the best beef and pork in town. You can even visit the meat case before you choose. If you show up on a Saturday night with a large party, be prepared for some "deliberately paced" service. When they are busy, you might wait for a drink refill a little longer than you'd like. But you will never be disappointed by the food and the atmosphere.

name: Sami Thomas
text: Amazing food with a great atmosphere! Try a designer cocktail or ask the bartender to whip up something with your favorite base. You won't be disappointed. Get the Mac and cheese.

resp.text: Thank you.  Cheers!

name: Susan Adams
text: Best burger in Bozeman, hands down. I've had it several times, and every time, with the exception of one time, it was perfection. And the one time it was overcooked, they offered to make another or buy it back. That's why I'm giving 5 stars. Delicious cocktails, but more expensive than most other restaurants.

resp.text: Thank you for the kind words and we are happy to hear that you like our burger!  Cheers!

name: Jennifer Pearson
text: Great atmosphere, great drinks, delicious food!

resp.text: Jennifer, thank you for the kind words.  Cheers!

name: Matt Matt
text: The place is nice, Doug is very helpful. Plus, we are enjoying ourselves very much. The atmosphere on the street hits the spot. You can do much worse than here. My vision was ok. It has good flavor, it was a bit cold. The potatoes had to be stabbed to stay on the fork.

name: Tron F
text: I really can't say enough how awesome this place is for a date. The food and service is always top quality. The consistency is frankly astounding. The menu changes with the season's...so refreshing!

resp.text: thank you for the kind words.  Cheers!

name: Joseph Schumacher
text: Great steaks, original apps, great bar.

resp.text: Thank you, Joseph! We are so glad you enjoyed your experience at Open Range. Cheers!

name: Emily Van Genderen
text: Incredible drinks, fantastic staff. I love coming here, always feel taken care of and welcome. The management really cares about their customers.

resp.text: Thank you for the kind words.  Cheers!

name: Joseph Bernhardt
text:
Open Range used to be one of my favorite places in town.  Their aged steaks were some of the best in the valley.  The prices were a bit high, but the food was well worth it.  Their drinks were always fun and delicious. This last time, however, was a completely different story.

We came here for my birthday, so I decide to splurge and get the Bartender's Choice drink special.  They no longer had the Old Fashioned flight that I used to love, so why not live on the edge, right?  What came back was dismal.  $15 for barely an ounce of indistinguishable liquor drowned in a cup of sugar.

I order the sirloin, as I had never been disappointed with it.  Again, it wasn't disappointing.  But, it also wasn't the best in the valley as it had been before.  It was just.... meh?  My wife's shrimp pasta was also very watery and bland.  I think the only thing that was really good was the side of brussel sprouts.  Although, the wife might argue otherwise.

I hate to say it, but I don't think I'm willing to risk returning after this experience.

resp.text: Joseph, I would love to chat with you about your experience personally.  I can be reached by phone at the restaurant most weeks, Monday-Friday at (406) 404-1940.  Call anytime between 2pm and 11pm.  My e-mail is Jason@openrangemt.com and can be reached in that way as well.  I would appreciate the opportunity to hear more detail about your meal.  I am sorry to hear that you were disappointed and if given the chance, I hope we can make amends.  - Jason Crume, General Manager, Open Range

name: Jay Szott
text:
I will start off saying the food was very good and cooked perfectly. That is the only positive thing I can say about this place.

The have a huge spirits and wine list but our server didn't know anything about it other than they few drink specials. They didn't have common spirits such as amaretto nor did our server even know what that was.

Secondly was prices versus portions. I ordered the seared ahi tuna and while it was cooked perfectly, it would barley feed a child. I am okay with a smaller portion but they should have some sides with it to prevent you from going hungry.

Also they up charged for every single thing. Extra sauce, one dollar, nuts on your ice cream, one dollar. That's a little excessive when two scoops of ice cream costs 9 dollars. Make that a Sunday for 15!

For the price this is not a good value. Go somewhere else on main, spend the same money but actually leave full.

name: Jared Frasier
text:
This is now my go-to for when I have friends in town.  Everything is right: Location, staff treatment, ambiance, menu, and especially the drink options.

Also, the crowd is a lot less rowdy than many of the other places in town.  It feels hi-brow, but the price still agreeable.

I noticed a fair amount of the staff behind the bar and waiting on tables are some of the best talent that was at other establishments in town as well.  Whatever they are doing on the HR side, they've got it figured out.

name: Tim Nicholson
text:
Excellent environment for a classic dinner, but if I'm paying 39 bucks for a sirloin I should not have to send it back because it was not cooked
Properly.

name: Matt Semple
text: Amazing steak great atmosphere.

name: Eric Karshner
text: Open Range provides a nice casual atmosphere serving high quality steaks. All of our steaks were cooked exactly as we ordered them. The rib eye was fantastic and the filet melted in your mouth. A nice touch is that you can view the steaks in a butcher-style cooler prior to ordering.The Mac N' Cheese and mushroom side dishes were also very good and complimented the steaks well. The service was no nonsense but they were attentive to our needs. Highly recommend Open Range for date night or celebrating a special occasion.

name: Steve Rast
text: Delicious. Steaks and beverages.  Prices are slightly inflated.

resp.text: Thank you for the kind words.  Cheers!

text: Edit 2020: “Still the best dinner in Bozeman. Highly recommend the special (always something new), fresh and delicious.” Best dinner and/or cocktail in Bozeman. For dinner, their beef is unmatched. And for drinks, their bar tenders have the most unique and skilled recipes in the state.

resp.text: Thanks Dylan, we'll keep trying.

name: AJ Koenes
text:
We were disappointed with the service. It took 10-20 minutes to put our order in, and the restaurant was only 1/4 full. Once we had the order in, and it took 30 minutes to recieve the food. Once my streak arrived, I couldn't believe how little meat 🥩 there was, flavor was lacking, and it was tough.
Maybe being born in Bozeman gives me different expectations, and I expect a well marbled steak that makes a good meal. I don't go to a steak house to fill up on salad and potatoes.

name: Cody Jerry
text: Incredible food and great service. Have been here twice, and loved both times.

resp.text: Thank you for the kind words.  Cheers!!

text: Fun motel.. Good location and dog friendly.

name: george bloomgren
text: It was short on execution for quality food.to reach the expectations of the price they would need to have a chef instead of a line cook that probably was fired from ihop.most dissatisfaction for 300 I have had in a long time.

name: Dean S
text: Good steak as you would expect but not much else on the menu.

name: Jana Cichowski
text: Great concept and good food, but if you have any special dietary restrictions, be prepared to pay more for what you need to change/substitute. Though I was impressed with my food, I have repeatedly not been impressed with how they manage substitutions due to dietary restrictions. name: Jonathan Hilgeman
text:
I think Open Range is the best option in Bozeman for a great steak, and like most steakhouses, it's on the pricey side but you get what you pay for. Everything from the appetizers and sides to the entrees to the desserts and drinks - all is top-notch.

The cocktail menu is helpfully divided into sections based on your taste preferences so you can easily find something smoky and dark, based on a whiskey or bourbon, or something light and more likely to have mint or cucumbers or elderberry, etc...

The drinks change from time to time, which can be sad if they rotate out a favorite drink (such as the elaborate smoked cocktail I had there once), but most of the choices are good and the waiters are happy to help you select something.

They do have some dishes aside from steak, but if  you're going to go to a steakhouse... That said, I've tried a few (mostly as stolen bites from others' dishes) and they seem to do good job on what I've tried (the chicken, the burgers, etc).

The highlight is really the steaks, of course. I'm normally the ribeye guy, so my steak is typically the more expensive choice on the menu (roughly $40 to $45) but it's a beautiful cut of meat each time and perfectly prepared. I don't usually add any special toppings - it is delicious with it's normal seasonings - but there is an array of choices like shrimp or mushrooms or various sauces.

They will also respect your order and cook the steak to your request, which is a welcome change from most steakhouses where the chef will opt to leave a bit of pink when someone requests a well-done steak,  like my wife did when she was pregnant. Sure, it's not as tasty as medium-cooked, but it's good to have the customer's request honored exactly.

I would expect most bills run around $50 to $75 per person, depending on what else you order besides an entree and a drink.

name: Rob Stephens
text:
This is a newer,  beautiful restaurant from Jay Bently , who ran The Mint Bar & Cafe in Belgrade, MT for years very successfully. Having had many celebration dinners there, my niece wanted to try his new place in Bozeman. I Went with my sister, a friend and my niece for her 29th birthday.  While i was parking our vehicle,  the girl's went in to get seated. This being an UPSCALE restaurant with knowledgeable wait staff they were surprised that "one" of the hostesses (knowing my niece is a wheelchair user) tried to seat them via a staircase. ..hhmmm?? After she was told three times that wheelchairs CONNOT climb stairs, they asked her if there was a ramp to access the upper seating area were our table was....but  they were told NO. Turns out there IS a ramp!! I followed in about 5 min later and asked to be seated with my party & not knowing i was talking with a "different" hostess, i was told they had not checked in or had been seated yet so i had her take me to our table anyway...SURPRISE, there they were already seated!!
Ok , so the "hostess" who seated the girls at first couldnt figure out that wheelchairs can't climb stairs and to note that we had arrived for our reservation.... things got better but not GREAT (we think she may have been drunk). Our waitress introduced herself,  took drink orders & told us of the nightly specials. Being on the busy side drinks didn't take too long but she did forget to bring the Tea ordered for one of us. Dinner orders were placed and our shared appetizers arrived while i was using the restroom. My niece thoroughly enjoyed her Escargot but our cheese plate came with ONE piece of bread for 3 people...hhmmm? Upon returing from the restroom (and then ordering more bread) i was just starting to enjoy our starter when a busgirl began clearing the other's appetizers dishes and asked to clear mine...i said i was still eating and asked her not too. Entrees arrived shortly thereafter and the busgirl just took away the appetizer i was still working on , so i just gave up my plate...hhmmm ? A signature item of thier's, the Ribeye Steak arrived NOT done to order, but the problem was fixed and were delicious!! My sister & our friend "split" a steak and therefore ordered extra sides (due to the bread incident) not knowing the split came wih full portions which might have been usefull information from our waitress. We then asked for the Dessert menu after our dinner and it had some great choices. We each decided on what we wanted only to find out our choices were sold out....once again, that would have been some useful information beforehand !! Away from the table I asked our waitress to bring my niece a "surprise" dessert
(including a candle) i picked out for her, but then put out silverware first..... OOP'S, there goes the surprise!. The girls loved it but my niece didnt like the sound of the Smoked Peach Creme Brulee with Candied Bacon that i ordered for her and decided on an EXCELLENT homemade chocolate icecream. The place is beautiful with high arched wooden cielings, fun (a bit loud) music playing, LOTS of black & white photos of LOCAL pet dogs (bring in a pic & they'll put up yours too!) and It was a very nice evening, but for the prices paid ($$$$) they should be doing a much better job and have staff properly trained in ALL aspects of fine (casual) dining. I have had many fine meals at Mr. Bently's prior restaurant,  but i am still struggling to justify the price of our bill ($210 for 3 entrees, 6 drinks, 2 desserts) compared to the level of service recieved. Perhaps "biting" off more than he could chew..... I do hope it was just an off night for Jay and his crew!!!.

text:
When I called to make reservations for our second visit to OpenRange, I mentioned that the evening would be my wife's birthday celebration. When we were escorted to our booth, we found a bouquet of beautiful roses on the table, as well as a gift certificate birthday present. Nice welcome!
Dinner was superb. We started with the grilled (yes, grilled) Ceasar salad. You need to experience this imaginative and delicious take on the classic dish. We both had the same entree - the tenderloin (filet mignon) of bison, done perfectly medium rare and more tasty than a similar cut of beef. It came with smoked mashed potatoes which were a perfect complement, and baby broccoli heads. On an impulse we ordered creamed spinach. It came in a cast iron frying pan serving dish to keep the sauce warm. Sauce was white chedar cheese, cream, peper and, we think, a hint of nutmeg. Delicious. We finished with the strawberry-watermelon cake, far more interesting than creme brulee! And I had the French press coffee, rich without being so strong that it overtook the flavors of the cake.
Service was prompt without being pushy. The sound level of the room was wonderful. The restaurant and bar were full and lively, but we could speak quietly and hear each other easily.
A perfect birthday dinner, and we had the time on the way out to engage the manager in conversation and thank him for arranging the flowers and gift certificate.
We have eaten in restaurants on five continents, and this one ranks right up there with places like the Commander's Palace (James Beard's place) in New Orleans. This is THE place in Bozeman. Make reservations or be prepared for a long, long wait.

text: Orange chicken was pretty good, jasmine fried rice was bland and kinda icky, egg roll had a weird flavor and wasn’t crispy, and the cream cheese wontons were decent.

name: Brian Vincent
text: Good food, good atmosphere

name: kai hogen
text: This is my favorite place to get fresh fast Chinese food in town

name: Jessica Moran
text:
I have updated my rating of SC2 from two stars to three stars and would describe the food establishment as a refreshing experience for Bozeman when it comes to  fastfood.

I first was excited about SC2 because I really enjoy their sister restaurant Sweet Chill downtown. Though I was quickly disappointed when I first walked in because it is vastly different than their sister restaurant.
SC2 is a curry based restaurant and the serving style is set up like panda express.
The first dish I tried was a bison curry with cream cheese wontons. Honestly the bison curry was unpleasant and "gross." I wouldn't  put a meat like bison in a curry, but i look forward to trying the veggie curry and the wontons I ordered were delicious. Anytime I go to Panda Express for wontons they are out, (everytime!) But SC2 always has food hot and ready.
The first time I came into SC2 the service was atrocious, due to the lack of menu and product knowledge. It was also bad customer service to not inform customers of deals and then tacking on frivolous extra charges, especially when the food is already expensive for fast food.
Since my first review, I have returned to find that the customer service has improved in friendliness and they have knowledge of their product menu.
I asked the server what she liked the best on the menu and so suggested a delicious item.
Also they have bubble tea; and though they are not my favorite place to go for bubble tea, they are able to deliver much more quickly than other places and it is still delicious.

To sum up my experience;
Im happy with the improvements and SC2 is a nice place to checkout for "something different"

name: Amy Mountain Ference
text: Among my favorite spots in Bozeman to grab a bite, and the quality is by far the best! Especially love the General Tsao and the Panang curry, but I've tried most and enjoy it all. Great quality for the price- the two mains with a base might be the best lunch deal in Bozeman!

text: Our experience at Blackbird was very memorable. Amazing food, friendly wait staff, cozy atmosphere, and safe covid policies. We had multiple appetizers and entrees - everything tasted fantastic! And even better, when receiving the check I was shocked at how reasonable the price was. This place is a must stop!

name: Lotus
text:
I remember the gourmet flavors of yore.
It's still very charming and the service is still so friendly and stupendous.  The antipasto options ARE scrumptious but the entrees are over reliant on salt. ❤ I've  never had a bad wine bottle. It is a small but well curated selection. budino ❤ pie

name: Steven Guzman
text:
An incredible place.  We visit West Yellowstone every year and this year we decided to stay in Bozeman for a day. A friend suggested this place.

First of all, I am a former employee of Danny Meyer's restaurant group Union Square Hospitality Group while working at Blue Smoke. I also live in Jersey City at this place called Razza which was given a great review from NY Times Restaurant Critics Peter Wells.  Also owned by a former USHG Alumni.

After eating here, I felt like I was back home.

The ambiance was amazing with a rustic open kitchen look and great music vibes.

The food....Amazing.  We had the Rabbit Liver Pate that was accompanied with picklend red onions, seeded mustard and crostini.  2 Kale Salads to share as well as 2 Parsnip Pansott.  We shared everything. The Cheese Plate was amazing.

We had 2 pizzas.  The Mostarda is the Rave but the Bianca was my favorite.

An amazing place that everyone should experience.

PS: we were a party of five but great place to do a date night.

name: Dylan Weber
text: Great food, wine, and atmosphere. Love this place.

name: Amy Deines
text: Ate here during there weekly night fair, so had the bonus of some local music to listen to, while we ate some truly amazing pizza and a cheese board with a blue cheese to die for. The cab wine the waitress suggested went perfectly with it all.  One of my traveling companions had a pasta dish and liked it but ended up stealing some pizza. All in all the pizza won the night!

name: Chloe Alix
text: Delicious! Incredible pizza and apps. Very friendly service.

name: C L
text: I have been dining here at least 25 times over the past several years. The kale  salad is always a favorite along with the Speck pizza.  This visit we also had the delicata squash and the ricotta ravioli.  This time (and on our previous visit) the Budino dessert recipe has changed and though still good not as delectable as in the past so hence the 4 stars

name: Chris Miller
text: We were gifted a night out at Blackbird and boy was it a great gift. We had a great bottle of wine which complemented the beet salad, salumi board and onion pizza perfectly. I am a restaurant chef who has worked for some very high end clubs and I have to applaud the execution of the kitchen staff. The only complaint I had the entire night was that our second course arrived before our wine. If that's the worst I can experience then this place deserves 5 stars and a glowing recommendation. Great job guys.

name: Theo Petersen
text: Awesome place. Everything on the menu is good, no matter what you get. As a college student, I don't go out to eat very much but Blackbird is definitely worth every cent. Plus,  everyone that works here is very involved with the outdoor community within Bozeman.

name: Olivia Simas
text: I’m from NY and this is some of the best pizza I’ve ever had 🤤

name: Joseph Schumacher
text: Very fun atmosphere, we celebrated a birthday here. Olives, bread, and a sulami board to start. Everyone had pizza while I opted for a delightful pasta dish. Everyone raved about the kale salad.

name: Jessie May Campbell
text: Blackbird is our go to restaurants for special occasions and a meal we can't stop talking about. Their daily designed menu focuses on the freshest local ingredients. Who knew parsnips would make such a mouthwatering appetizer!?!

name: Cory Lagor
text: Awesome food. Love their pizzas and kale salad (and I'm normally not a fan of kale). Wait can be kind of long, but worth it; best to just make a reservation.

text: The service was great, meatball app was delicious, but for a place specializing in pizza... The pie was garbage...

text: A little pricey

name: Ray Linsky
text: I was genuinely impressed eating here. Bozeman has an overabundance of "boutique" restaurants...all show, small portions, exorbitant pricing. Not at this establishment! Unique, flavorful combinations, fair priced. I would definitely recommend them for diners that want a different dining experience.

name: Richard Murphy
text: Favorite restaurant in Bozeman!!!! SO good! Everything about it. The bread app is incredible. The veggies are delightful. The pizza is the star here!!! Wood fire, amazing combinations! The crust is perfect every time. Great wine list. Great service. Great atmosphere. Run here!!!!

name: Karl Molina
text: I got the braised beef short ribs, they were good so was the polenta that came with them. I will want to try something else next time though. The bread was good.

name: Kathy Randle
text: Awesome chefs with an open kitchen. The staff and the food where amazing.

name: Tyler Sacre
text:
This place was amazing!

Food was great (especially the bread)!!

4/5 stars because the service was questionable. There were two times - when one of our friends didn’t get his beer and when refills weren’t brought to the table.

Otherwise, good experience.

name: constantine vorobetz
text: Awesome and unique!  Highly recommend this place.  It's a Bozeman favorite for me.

name: Cristina Chiotti
text: Consistently delicious and always exceeding expectations ! We enjoyed seasonal plum dishes including the upside down plum cake, phenomenal!

name: Steve Olp
text:
One of the best Restaurants in Bozeman.
Food is very consistent in its deliciousness. You really should try the Kale salad. Specials are very good and the wine list is adequately sized and properly eclectic. Small and intimate, not great for very large groups but very good for small groups of 4. Slow turns at these tables and a reservation is a good idea. For couples or walk ins try the bar or the small tables. Bathroom is through a labyrinth but it is back there I promise. Desserts and espresso are nice if you're craving something light. Extremely well executed and some of the best bread in town, which in and of itself may not seem like a big deal but it really is.

name: Larry Combs
text: Creative menu and great setting.

name: Susan Adams
text: One of my favorites in town. So delicious and fresh. I love sitting at the bar and watching them make the pizza. It's a great place to just take your time, order several courses and enjoy a night out. Service and food have always been equally wonderful.

name: Todd Buckley
text:
Such amazing place!! Nice vintage vibe, lovely staff answered all my questions with a smile. Food was fantastic, totally worth the wait all week!! Food was delicious!!  Make a reservation you won't regret it!!

The owner's of Blackbird are fantastic people as well!!! Great place I'll be back again!!!

name: Lori Fitzgerald
text:
Service was prompt and friendly. The Blackbird Bread with Olive Oil would have been a great starter, but they failed to appropriately season the olive oil, and the wood fired bread was burnt black on the bottom  The Pasta Agnolotti was out of this world wonderful... All four bites of it. Really. Seriously.The sirloin was beautifully seasoned. Unfortunately, it was only a perfect medium temperature on the inside. The outside was crusted to a very crunchy well-done.....All four bites of it. What was supposed to be an 8oz sirloin was cooked down to about 4 oz., and it was sliced into four very small medallions.

European prices. Even smaller than European portions. Far less than European quality.

I spent my down time (when I wasn't eating the food that I had hoped would fill my plate but didn't) fantasizing that the Blackbirds would swoop down and attack in a very Hitchcock-like fashion. In my fantasy, I would then grab a few of those avian delicacies, slap them on the grill, and have a real meal!!!!

name: Kory Sutherland
text: Excellent Italian food, wood fired pizza, and selection of wine and beer. The Blackbird house-made bread is incredibly good, and enough for your whole table. Best Kale salad I've ever had. Outstanding service in a packed restaurant on a Saturday night. Wish the menu had more pasta options. Overall fantastic experience and cuisine!

name: Sarah B
text: Honestly, the salad was small for the price and my glass of wine seemed less than the person next to me. But they do have great food and the ambiance is very nice.

name: Douglas Crumpler
text: Grest food and very professional and gracious staff

name: Felix
text: The food is good. Nobody died. Injuries were not apparent. The waiter and I kissed.

name: A Gordon
text: Always impressed with the food and they've expanded their options. Next time I'll be venturing away from the pizza to try the other tempting options now offered. It's been awhile since I was last there so not sure how long they've had a newer menu. The drinks list is pretty great too, they always have a couple ciders if you aren't looking for beer or wine. The staff there are great and always helpful with anything and everything you could ask. Seating can be tight because of how popular this place is and it's in a smaller space but it's never been a bad experience. Not ideal for super large groups but smaller groups can definitely meet up here. Great for couples. Always recommend.

text: Really good pizza, definitely would come here again, the dessert we got was apple pie. Very small wouldn't have a big party. Definitely a place for 1-4 people max.

name: Kathy Randle
text: If you go their have the Lamb Chops!!!! Awesomeness!!!! You guys rock!!!!!

name: Shannon Arthur
text: The burrata is worth the trip!  Fantastic place for a leisurely meal.

name: Lauren Summers
text:
We went for my birthday with a big group and shared a bunch of pizza's and the kale salad. Every single pizza was delicious
They even made a vegan pizza special for my friend. The wine carafe of sangiovese was tasty and fun to share. It was a fun environment and a great place for a date or special occasion.

name: poop mcgee
text: Eaten here twice, had the lamb first time and Speck pizza the second time. Lamb was perfectly cooked and delicious. Pizza ingredients & dough were very well prepared and high quality. 10/10 will eat here again

name: Laine McNeil
text: A unique kind of pizza place. Very different pizza than you find at most other places, with unusual but very tasty combinations. Thin crust, hand tossed & baked in an oven that you can sometimes sit near to warm up in winter. Other good food options too, of course. Gnocchi, meat dishes (chicken & other).

name: Ted Coté
text: My absolute favorite restaurant in Bozeman. From their selection of wines to the simple, fresh menu that offers flavorful pasta dishes, amazing wood-fired pizzas. The best pizza is the 'panna'. Desserts are always unique and delicious. Difficult to get a table without a reservation, but well worth the effort.

name: Jared Frasier
text: The wood fired pizza is quite good.  The atmosphere is very casual.  Some folks are dressed up for a night out, others area wearing shorts and flip flops after a day of work.  The service staff are also friendly and helpful.  I showed up after helping at a show in the Emerson and they had just closed.  The head of house let me in anyway and took great care of us - despite the closed sign.

name: Elo Nielsen
text: Best restaurant in Bozeman. Best bread in my life (and I'm from France). Quiet and warm atmosphere. Very good quality food and cooking. Nice service.

name: Kirkwood Donavin
text:
Delicious Italian food including brick-oven pizza and savory rice and pastas. Cool urban atmosphere with windows facing the street and low-lighting. Open kitchen offers a lively experience.

This place is expensive but worth a try on a special night.

name: Patrick Gescheidle
text: Delicious food, romantic atmosphere. Great for date night!

name: Steven Van Pelt

name: Matthew Buenrostro
text: Kind,  excellent staff.  And the bianca is the best pizza i have EVER eaten

name: Chase Massey
text: Good place for a fancy date. Awsome staff and amazing fired pizza

name: Brenna Szott
text: Based on reviews, and other people's testimonies, I was truly looking forward to dining here. Overall, the food was mediocre. We got sat right away which was great since it was a Friday and we didn't have reservations. Took a bit for our server to come by, but when she did, offered either flat or sparkling water. I thought this was a nice touch and wasn't an additional cost. I started with the marinated olives, which were quite good, and has fresh oregano and fennel within the olives. Good portion and only $5. I ordered the burrata margherita pizza and my husband ordered the tajarin. My pizza was beyond soggy and barely had any cheese. Burrata is an amazing cheese and I was expecting it to be added at the last minute to be able to break into it. That wasn't the case. Instead it was fully melted and again had like 4 small pieces on the entire pie. The pizza was a good size and the crust was fantastic but the sauce was basically an unflavored watery tomato sauce that penetrated the crust which lead to limp pizza. I tried to pick it up and the cheese would slide right off. Should have just gotten the regular margherita pizza. Probably would have been the same but no up charge for the non-existent burrata. My husband's pasta was more of a lunch portion than anything. Small amount of what seemed like homemade pasta, which was good, but not worth the amount of money for the 3 bites he was given. The meatballs were dry and not much flavor. A bit too salty as well. We spent a lot of money on food that was sub par and waited an hour and a half to get said food. Our server was decent but didn't really interact with us at all. Overall, would not return.

name: Megan
text: I was thrilled that the Blackbird staff was able to seat me at the bar, even during peak dinner hours. The place was absolutely packed, but honestly, the best seat in the joint is for the walk-ins. Watching the chefs work is entertaining and almost lyrical. The rhythm and coordination in the kitchen is endlessly fascinating. My favorite bit was watching them tip the pizza's cheese to the fire inside the oven and then seeing it come out bubbling and browned. Every single bite of food was delicious to beat. I had the margherita pizza, but split the roasted broccoli as an appetizer. The peppers in the roasted broccoli get my award for the night - they were incredible.

name: Pancasatya Agastra
text: The closest thing to the Italian pizza in Bozeman and it is a premium pizza. The place is really romantic with the dim light. If you are a pizza lover, you ought to try their pizza.

name: Ryan Johnson
text: Second time here, everything is excellent. The service was above and beyond. This is my favorite spot, and that's saying a lot because there are so many high quality restaurants in Bozeman.

name: John McParland
text: Flawless dinner from top to bottom... don't expect to just waltz in the front door and eat tho...Make a reservation, especially for 3+ in your party. And there's a reason it's that way, because the food is the toppest of notches. Kale salad and margherita pizza for the win

name: Pricsilla Cervantes
text: Had pizza with a fried egg on it ! Life changing! Great wine list!

name: Rachel Gavin

text:
Didn't let me in?

It was 8:50pm and this guy just told me to leave. Wouldn't seat me. Said they were closed.

Let in more people after me as I was leaving.
Was not polite at all. I was well spoken and well dressed. I called ahead to ask if I could come in and they said yes.

Very very bad first impression.
Starting a boycott

text: A super cute, intimate place to grab pizza in a nice environment at the heart of Main street (think "date night", not your typical pizza joint). The food is delicious, the prices are fairly reasonable, and the service is usually pretty good. Be aware that it can be hard to get a seat without a reservation on weekend nights.

P.S: You can purchase loaves of their break for $8!

name: Sam Haraldson

name: Beth Schecher
text: I just stayed 3 nights at The Lindley House.  Alison was a warm and friendly host and clearly loves the hospitality business.  The accommodations are top notch.  Although it is an old house, it has been renovated so that you feel the old world charm and have modern conveniences.  Everything feels new and fresh.  If you can't arrive in the designated check-in times (like me) just let them know and they will send you specific instructions on letting yourself in and getting settled.  I stayed in one of the 2nd floor rooms, but if stairs are not your thing, there is also a room on the first floor.

resp.text: We love the way the renovation turned out and it's great to hear that you do too! We hope you get a chance to return.

name: lisa turley
text: Cozy. Private. Close to downtown bars & eatery. Only issue might be parking. Would stay again.

resp.text: So glad you enjoyed your stay. Our neighborhood has on street public parking so it's open parking anywhere on the street around our big corner home which has worked well for guests.

name: Nick Byma
text: Can't say enough great things about The Lindley House. We thoroughly enjoyed the hospitality of Alison. Great breakfast, comfy bed, and great style throughout the house. Walking distance from downtown made it nice to get dinner and drinks on Main St. Thanks again, we'll be back!

resp.text: We enjoyed having you here and hope to see you on your next visit!

name: Cynthia Thomas
text: Very quant, cozy place to stay. The owners/hosts of this bed and breakfast are wonderful! I highly recommend staying here.

name: Raf Viniard
text:
Very disappointed this time, previous visits it was worth the 2 hour drive...this time not so much.

Made reservations earlier in week, get there and they seat us next to the kitchen below the vent fan in the back room having a birthday party.

The kids menu is perfect for kids and also adults who aren’t looking to eat a big dinner.  The hot wings are the BEST I have ever had. Jeff, the chef,  has been a respected chef since I was a kid and his food is a gift for us to enjoy.  I would highly recommend you try it and do yourself a favor and book at a reasonable time like between 5-6 or 8 and later if you want a little more peace and quiet. You won’t be disappointed.

name: J Foster

Jagz is more than twice the distance (25+ miles) for us to drive than where we usually go to dine out. When we walked in nobody acknowledged our presence for 12 minutes however every single front of house employee walked by us in that time frame.

Once we were seated we ordered their nicest bottle of Pinot Noir ($99) which was very good. Our server was on her fifth shift and knew nothing of the menu and didn't make an effort to ask the kitchen my questions. I ordered the New York and my wife the Filet. Both our meals came out cooled off. The steaks must have been sitting at the window 10+ minutes. My wife is pregnant and specified she needed her Filet cooked well done, It was cooked medium rare at best. My New York was ordered medium rare and was cooked to order.

Overall not a terrible experience but considering their quality of service and price point we will continue frequenting Spencer's and Whitefish Lake Golf Course for our steak nights.

The charbroil grill they use gives your steak that nice cinge!! Its so good.  If you are one of those people who doesn't like noise, might I suggest eating at home. 99% of restaurants are noisy. Jagz has a semi classy atmosphere, fireplace, twinkle lights, water served in wine glasses yet has a very laid back feeling. Come as you are and eat and be treated like royalty!! name: Brian Friess
text: Kalispell is a desirable destination town in Northwest Montana. it has seen a lot of pressure over the decades from people who want to move here.  It has Scenic views, warm hospitable native people, and us a jumping off place to experience some natural wonders.  it is constantly growing and expanding so hopefully we can see some Healthy Growth and Community Development over the next decade or so. but at the moment the housing market is being pressed hard from people who want to live in a place that doesn't have a large population. the culture here is very family based and based in love and Common Sense and a keen awareness their consciences, God, faith, hope, and grace.

Amazing. I hiked to Avalanche Lake which took somewhere between 1-2 hours at a brisk walk. The trail was surprisingly populated. It isn't a short trail but it was busy. The trail was well maintained but isn't all level or remotely even. Bring some proper footwear. Also remember your water.
Avalanche Lake was so beautiful. Surrounded by mountains and the water is crystal clear.
I would recommend bringing a snack or lunch or even some whiskey. Hike in to the lake and take a few minutes to sit on a log and just look at it.
Definitely worth your time if you are capable of hiking.
Stay on the trails.

name: Brian Friess
text: The Flathead National Forest is really a vague and vast amount of land owned by the federal government and managed by federal employees.  There are still great  chunks of land that are managed well that are beautiful and provide  ample opportunities for outdoor activities to be enjoyed by all.  unfortunately in more recent days this has led to a number of road closures and blockages that prevent the public use of lands that were originally meant for the people. I'm not sure how the government of the United States became something other than "of the People by the people and for the people" but it's clear that many situations such as these indicate that the government is something other than "for the people".

name: Greg Krudener
text:
The trees are all bending
In one direction
Because of something
Is a beautiful thing.
Oh when the sun goes down,
The fireflies come out.
Pity the mate of Queen Mantis,
So content, but so headless.
Katy did nothing but shiver and cry,
As did the dragonfly.
In the shade the gypsies spin
Among the cloves, they drop their skin.
beyond the hedge grove,
Over by the willows,
Deep in the shadows
Regeneration occurs at a furious speed
Beneath the white oak tree.
And when the sun comes up
Moon buds fold up.
In the sun she warmed her wings
ain't ever seen it, but I have heard it.
Sounds like the millstones when they are turning,
But every moment getting louder and louder,
And then there is silence,
And the smell of flowers.

name: Mark-Kayla Dalimata
text: Small local business with big local selection! Affordable prices for fishing gear, hunting gear, clothes, guns, ammo, shoes, sandals, boots, snow gear.....AMAZING SALES! Positive contributions to our Valley! Amazing staff! Friendly, helpful, and personable. If they don't have what you need, they will try their hardest to get it for YOU! Making you feel like a special customer. They really are an amazing, beneficial business in our Valley. Favorite place to shop for all my fishing, hunting, and outdoor needs! Even for my kids! They have a Santa and do photos for kids, and last I knew they have a pond for kiddos to fish and catch fish! You just cant beat Snappy's. Really gives bigger Outdoor businesses a run! Small but AMAZING!!!!!

name: Gary Lowrance
text: Owned by a retired US Navy Veteran, Snappy's has one of the finest fishing departments in the country as well as full service firearms sales and support. When you add all of the sporting good supply with a friendly and knowledgeable staff, Snappy's is my first stop for sports needs in the Flathead Valley. The fact that we support a local business that is very active in local sponsorship of sporting events leads me to think it should be everyone's first stop for sporting goods!!!

name: Elvia Hun
text: I went in to buy a kayak but they didn't have any. I guess it's too late to get one? That's on though,we found a ton of lures to choose from at good prices. Went hog wild picking them. Also found nice sunglasses with decent price tags. I'll be going back.

resp.text: Hello Elvia, this year certainly has been rough for kayaks (and water toys in general). Usually this time of year I am getting down to the end, but will still have a couple hanging around. This year, NOTHING. We saw the rush hit early and fast. We placed additional orders and those went blasting out as well. Tried to contact our suppliers and they didn't eve have product to sell. I am sorry that we didn't have any options for you, but this summer has just blown everyone up. We are already looking for the fall activities though and are hoping for a great fall to recreate.

name: Ryan Nelson
text: Been shopping here since I was a youngster. They have pretty much all the gear needed to hunt fish or do camping or water activities.  They don't have any winter ski gear beyond gloves and clothes nor do they have a rock climbing section. It's a huge store but they don't have it all so I rarely go in anymore. Maybe one day they will see this demand in the valley.

resp.text: Hi Ryan, you are correct that we do not have it all. The Flathead is blessed with many great specialty shops who focus on one or two things and do them very well. Unfortunately you have found a couple of the areas that we haven't put our foot into. We certainly try and cover as many activities as we can, but there are many logistic parts to everything. Winter Skiing/Snowboarding is covered so well in the valley there is already a lot of overlap in this arena. I will certainly mention the rock climbing to our team... we haven't heard much demand on that front here in the store. There are a couple of local business that we refer the occasional request about this to as they have the knowledge and experience. We are always looking to see what is needed and I certainly appreciate your feedback. I hope that should you need anything for Fishing, Hiking, Camping or Hunting you would be sure to look us up.

text: Best fishing outfitter in town, hands down. Massive inventory of tackle and equipment. The staff is friendly, knowledgeable and will take the time to show you how to rig up and where to go. If you're having trouble, bring in your tackle box and they will help you make sense of it. Anytime I'm looking for something specific, they have it. Come here first and you won't need to go anywhere else. text: If you're buying a firearm online, take time to read the fine print in Snappy's internet website. The prices listed in their extensive list are Davidson Firearm wholesalers prices, which can be purchased through your favorite local dealer and save money. Snappy's is just a middle man.....

resp.text:
Our online Firearm store is indeed powered by Davidson’s Inc. We are able to offer their enormous inventory and selection to our customers. The prices offered online are exactly what you will pay for that firearm by purchasing it through our portal. Davidson’s will take a down payment and ship your firearm to Snappy’s so that all federal and state paperwork can be completed. This is standard practice as firearms cannot be shipped to a private party and must be shipped to a FFL dealer. The balance of the price presented to you on the portal is paid in store after completing the paperwork. There is no fee or price increase at the store level. That is the benefit of using our portal with Davidson’s. You see the price right online. The prices listed with Snappy’s/Davidson’s are very competitive.

If you have any questions or issues with pricing you have seen or with a gun that you purchased through Snappy’s/Davidson’s portal, please let me know and I’d be happy to look into this for you. Snappy’s is happy to offer this service to our community and offer a much larger selection of firearms available for purchase are fantastic prices.  Again, if you have any questions or an issue that I can address, please let me know.   Jon – Snappy’s

name: Kimberly Johnson
text:
In August of 2011 we purchased a rifle from Snappy's, patiently waited for it to come in and once we were out in the woods we discovered that it wouldn't cycle the ammunition.  Frustrated beyond all belief we were given no option but to send the rifle in to the manufacturer...so stupid stupid us...we bought the other gun that my husband wanted.  This was a different brand and totally unrelated to the first gun but also brand new...and it happened again!  When we took the gun back to Snappy's the man at the gun counter offered to make it right by doing...NOTHING!

He did nothing more than to shrug his shoulders and tell us there was nothing that could be done...no store credit, not discount on a different gun...not one dang thing!  We explained that this wasn't the level of customer service that we had known there before and again he shrugged his shoulders.

We weren't expecting them to move heaven and earth, really we weren't but something...but had they done anything at all I wouldn't be here writing about them, trying to warn people.

Needless to say we will never be back to Snappy's, not for gun, clothes, supplies of any kind...EVER!

This is truly a BUYER BEWARE kind of store!

resp.text:
Kimberly,
I am sorry that you had such a poor experience. We have revamped our gun department from top to bottom. We have updated the look and feel, and we have corrected some of those behaviors that were NOT what Snappy's was all about. I would love to have you stop back in and check out our all new Gun Department under the new management of Randy and the other gun guys. They are a great group of people and I am sure you'd be pleasantly surprised about the changes.

text: This place is a bit out of the way from most places in Glacier and you need to traverse some unpaved roads to get there.  That being said it's definitely worth it. It's a beautiful bakery with some merchandise as well. I definitely recommend seeing it at least once. Make sure you try one of the famous huckleberry bear claws when you're there!

name: Katheryn Kingery
text: This is a one of a kind epic experience...an absolute MUST when visiting Montana.

name: JoAnne Owens
text: Funky mercantile and campground - cabins for rent and also tent sites. We had a fresh-out-of-the-oven huckleberry danish and a bear claw. We also had some of their sandwiches for a picnic lunch. There is also a cafe on site, but we didn't try that. They had a nice selection of beer in the mercantile also - sold by the can. Locally made crafts, t-shirts, etc.

resp.text: The danishes are the delicacy of the mercantile! The bakers put some extra love into those pastries...three days worth of love to be exact! We love provided our customers with quality baked goods and locally made items. Thank you for stopping by!

text: I love the look of the town very welcoming, the road to get up there maybe a little to extreme for small cars I was in a 4 wheel drive truck and im telling you it was rough. Was it worth it ???? Maybe if you could get a warm fresh out the oven huckleberry bear claw.YES, Unfortunately they wrap all the pastry in plastic wrap for me that didn't work. Soggy,not fresh tasting. Would love to try again fresh.

name: Christian
text: It’s a bit of a drive on dirt roads but worth the trip! Pretty good local bakery. Very cool location.

name: Rosie Jones
text:
What a fun place! It’s not too far from West Glacier and it’s on the way to the Canadian border. The bakery sells souvenirs and drinks as well as the pastries. We tried the huckleberry bear claw and it was delicious! The whole area was super cute and straight out of a time long gone by. We enjoyed the bear claw and sodas in a sitting area at the entrance.
Side note: the bathroom had a solid metal toilet. It had to have been near 100 degrees when we were there, but still that solid metal toilet was ice cold. I could still feel the shock of the cold on my bottom for the whole 20+ mile drive back to West Glacier!

name: Nick Deal
text: This place can be rough to get to with the roads but it is a really great experience if you come to glacier. They have a lot of Montana gifts and Montana made products. Their pastries are excellent, I recommend the nutella banana bear claw.

It just doesn't feel as touristy as other places. Make the drive.

resp.text: Thank you for the review Kristopher!

name: Kate Eaton
text: The bear claws are amazing, but at $5.50 a pop, definitely on the expensive side. Most everything in the store was outrageously priced, so there are definitely better places to get souvenirs. There are a few groceries if you are desperate and willing to pay three times more than normal.

resp.text: Hey Kate, we believe that the prices of our products match the beautiful scenery we are surrounded by. It's also important to take into consideration that we are over 35 miles away from the nearest city. It costs more money for us to get the products we need to make the best pastries while still being in an isolating location. We also emphasize the importance of supporting local artists which may seem over priced compared to other souvenir shops that mass produce. We think it's important to put our money back into our community and hope that our customers feel the same. Thank you for the review and we hope to see you again soon.

name: Peter Ro
text: It's a part of Glacier NP institution. To get there one has to drive on rough gravel road for 25+ minutes but it's worth the experience . I believe  I had the biggest bear's claw (their signature huckleberry pastry) ever. Even the employee conceded it was the biggest he had seen. Enjoying the pastry with huckleberry lemonade at the picnic table outside the store with cool wind blowing was   a savoring experience.

name: Lisle Pottorff
text: Classic destination in the Flathead Valley. Remote entrance to a relatively unvisited part of Glacier NP nearby. The Mercantile bakery is a must visit if you go. We like to take visitors our guests there because it is so unique.

name: B
text:
We stopped here on a very rainy July 4th, 2019.  Family of 6 in a white van (before we left) and totally orange from the muddy dirt road after.   We took the road from Columbia falls to polebridge through the Flathead national Forest then took the back entrance into Glacier national Park after.

The bakery is wonderful. Watch however the 2.5 percent surcharge when using a credit card and a 4 percent "renewable energy surcharge", neither of which did I notice any signs indicating the add-on charges.

We ordered several different types of pastries upon which I enjoyed the huckleberry claws.

The store has a myriad of items from soap to gasoline additives to coffee

Bring independance day, the place was packed with the festivities for the holiday. The rain did not seem to keep people away.

Well worth the visit.
Make sure you are prepared for no cellular service there.

resp.text: Thank you for the review B we greatly appreciate it!

name: J S
text: Always very friendly people there. And I certainly enjoy supporting the local community which is summer based only. They need us to support them plus the drive out their is exceptional. Yes the roads are a little rough, but slow down and enjoy the scenery and you won't even feel those bumps in the road.  Take a little time to drive up to the river behind the Mercantile north from the parking lot. There's a great deal of Rafters and kayakers and a little bridge to cross to see the river. One can do a little hiking out there. That is to say take the road right in front of the Mercantile to the north  and  behind the Mercantile up to the river. Plus there are two very short hikes just to the north, and within walking distance, of the parking lot.

resp.text: Hi Scott! We use the square system when checking people out and that system automatically displays the tip screen. name: Kristin Seeley
text: Hotel is still in good shape after 8yrs.  Stayed 5 nts. While burying my husband of 30yrs.  Spent more than $2,000. On multi rooms.  On 6th day only my sister and I are left scheduled to fly out the following AM.  That morning Emmitt GM called and said he was overbooked and we must check out.  We were devastated with the only place we could go was the floor at a family members home.  I was crushed emotionally and dumbfounded  by actions of the general general manager when I was told If I continued to stay he would call the local Police Dept to remove us because he was over booked.  It was at that point I began to reach out to Marriott corporate offices to get assistance only to be told if we pay $400.00 per night we can stay?  Elite Cust seer. Mgr Kim Summer Nebraska.  Marriott refused to help military widow while laying husband to rest retired Navy 30yrs 3 wars and wife thrown out by local PD bc $400.00 per night was not acceptable.  At least with over 5,000 views of this review I have been able to get the message across to respectable people who have chosen to stay elsewhere bc we all have choices.  How could I or anyone have possibly known what a poor excuse of a man in the hospitality business or GM Emmet Mathews would turn out to be.  The Helena police officers (all four) showed myself and my husband's memory a great deal of respect while completing what we felt was an unpleasant duty of escorting us from the hotel.  I often return to my husband's graveside and the sickening feeling I get each time I pass by the hotel leaves me in tears.  I was never offered any compensation what so ever from any upper management.  Nor has anyone ever disclosed the owner of this properties name or contact information.  Information I still welcome to this day over a year and a half since I laid my husband to rest.  Just about to hit the two year mark.  May we never forget.

resp.text:
Dear Mrs. Seeley,

I am the owner of the Helena Montana Residence Inn.  Your recent Google review was brought to my attention.  It contains some very serious allegations against our staff and so I have personally investigated your claims.

Let me start by expressing my condolences for the loss of your husband nearly two years ago.  I am sorry that this unfortunate event led to your visit.

The results of my investigation are as follows.
•	You originally booked a three night stay with us in April, 2018.  At the time of check-in, hearing of the unfortunate circumstances behind your visit, our staff gave you a complimentary room upgrade.
•	You inquired at that time about extending your stay.  Our staff advised you that we were fully booked for the nights following your original checkout date, and that we could only provide you a room after the third night if a reservation was cancelled.  You indicated that you understood and also that you had alternative lodging options in the area if needed.
•	We had reservation cancellations on the fourth and fifth nights, so you were able to stay both of those nights.
•	We did not have a room become available on the sixth night.  The staff informed you of this the day before.  A member of your party reacted by becoming publicly disruptive and abusive towards our staff.
•	On the morning of your sixth day with us, our staff confirmed to you that we could not offer you a room that night due to no reservation cancellations (we were fully booked).
•	You refused to leave.  You went to the room, locked the door and refused to vacate the premises.  The person sharing the room with you again became verbally abusive and threatening to our staff.
•	It was at this time that we called the police to ask them to escort you and your guest off the premises.  They did just that.

While we deeply regret that we had to involve the police, I do not apologize for the actions of our staff.  They did exactly what they should have done given the circumstances.  They went out of their way to try to accommodate your requests.  At the same time, they also have an obligation to provide promised rooms to our guests, just as they did for you with your original reservation.

I am very proud of the guest service record of our Helena staff.  This property has consistently ranked in the top 10-20% of all Residence Inns worldwide in terms of guest satisfaction scores.  Perhaps the best evidence of their excellent guest service and Mr. Matthew’s leadership comes from guest reviews received just today:

“The most comfortable place to stay wherever I go. Always super clean. Staff is awesome and always helpful and friendly… Home away from home!! Always great to stay here. Great staff and warm, welcoming atmosphere”.

“The staff were kind and accommodating during stressful times.”

“Great customer service provided. All the staff and housekeeping staff was good.”

While we regret that this incident occurred and you felt you were treated poorly, I stand by the actions of our staff.  I would be more than happy to discuss this matter directly with you.  If you wish to, please provide your contact information to the hotel and I will reach out to you.

Sincerely,

Robert Mahaney
